# Ledger item #1 — record proposal

Origin: ledger Phase 2 narrowing on #3401 (row 1)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`bin/flow-preflight.js` classifies a run directory as case 3 (adopted, pre-existing) whenever its `events.jsonl` is non-empty. On run `2026-10-17T190411-spec-3401` the self-minted directory held two `gate-exempt-gitignored` events before `config.yml` existed — both attributed from a sibling session's worktree (`dispatch-record-3405`) by the hook's fallback run-dir resolver — so a fresh mint was classified as an adoption. `/flow` Step 3 recovered by hand (treated it as case 2, wrote `config.yml` from the precedence chain, appended `decisions.md`), but nothing mechanical distinguishes "events this run produced" from "events a sibling misattributed here".

Cross-run event attribution to an empty mint is the hazard `flow/claim-targets.md` already names. The fallback resolver in `bin/lib/hooks/run-dir-resolve.js` picks the most recent matching run dir when `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` is unset in the hook's environment, which a sibling session's subagent shell routinely is. Refs #3401 (ledger row 1).

## Deliverables

`bin/flow-preflight.js` case classification treats `events.jsonl` as adoption evidence only when at least one event carries this run's own worktree or session (the `worktree`/`sessionId` fields `run-state.json` records), or when `config.yml` exists; an events file holding only foreign-attributed events classifies as case 2 and is reported as such in `preflight.json` (`eventsForeign: N`).

`bin/lib/hooks/run-dir-resolve.js`'s fallback never selects a run dir whose `run-state.json` names a different `worktree` than the hook's own resolved toplevel; when no run dir matches, it drops the event with a `sweep:`-style diagnostic to stderr instead of attributing it to the newest mint.

`tests/bin-lib/flow-preflight/*.test.js` and `tests/bin-lib/hooks/run-dir-resolve.test.js` each gain the foreign-events fixture: a freshly minted dir with two events from another worktree classifies case 2, and the resolver refuses the cross-worktree attribution.

## Acceptance Criteria

`node plugin/bin/flow-preflight.js --run {fresh-mint-with-foreign-events}` reports `case: 2` and `eventsForeign: 2`; with one own-worktree event it reports `case: 3`.

The hook resolver test fails when the worktree guard in the fallback is removed.

`npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Flow: a freshly minted run directory is no longer mistaken for an adoption because a sibling session's hook events landed in it first.

Origin: SDD controller final-review finding on #3401 (run 2026-10-17T190411-spec-3401)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

#3401 (run 2026-10-17T190411-spec-3401) made a load-bearing SDD `Ruling:` line a Pending-review row (`staged/sdd-ruling-{N}.md`, `open` ledger row) with ratify/reverse semantics defined for the single-spec chat console only: `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console-appendix.md`'s `sdd-ruling-*` bullet (ratify = `apply` → ledger `accepted`; `reverse` → born-ready reversal record + ledger `deferred`), `review-console-interactive.md`'s Override vocabulary (`ratify {#}` / `reverse {#}`, bare `skip` refused), and `review-console.md` step 1's pointer clause. Under `integration-model: pr-first` with a live PR — the default surface — `review-console-interactive.md` routes rendering to `_shared/console-on-pr.md` and never renders "Present the console"; on the PR, the legend (`console-on-pr.md` ~line 80) and `wrap-up/console-execution.md` (~line 47) treat an unticked item as **declined**, and the chat accelerator `resolve-console --approve {ids} --decline {ids}` (`console-execution.md` ~line 99) has no reverse slot. `flow/multispec-review-console.md` step 1 (~line 138, patches only) and its Override "skip" (~line 152) have the same gap for multi-spec runs, whose per-spec builds stage `spec-{N}/staged/sdd-ruling-*.md`. Result today: a human who unticks a ruling on the PR console to reverse it gets a logged decline, no reversal record, and the row stays `open` (caught later by the nothing-left-behind gate — loud, not silent — but the decision is lost). Found by #3401's whole-branch review (Important #1); #3401's Key Files scoped the record to the chat console, so this was deferred rather than folded into its one fix wave.

## Deliverables

`_shared/console-on-pr.md`: an `sdd-ruling-*` row's label carries its two dispositions, and the legend states what an unticked `sdd-ruling-*` item means at Resolve time (reverse — never a bare decline), citing `review-console-appendix.md`'s `sdd-ruling-*` bullet for the write-back.

`wrap-up/console-execution.md`: `resolve-console --decline` on an `sdd-ruling-*` id routes to reverse (compose the reversal record per the appendix bullet, ledger row → `deferred`), never to a plain decline; state it beside the existing decline semantics.

`flow/multispec-review-console.md`: step 1 and the Override vocabulary cite the appendix `sdd-ruling-*` bullet so a multi-spec run's `spec-{N}/staged/sdd-ruling-*.md` rows get ratify/reverse, and `skip` on one is refused the same way the single-spec console refuses it.

Add `reverse` to `review-console-interactive.md`'s Override option description (~line 52) and the Pending review heading's vocabulary so the human learns it before the refusal message; define `modify {#}`/`revert {#}` on a ruling row as refused the same way `skip` is.

Pin each prose addition in `tests/build-sdd-ledger-residue-carryforward.test.js` (or a sibling conformance suite) with go-red discrimination.

## Acceptance Criteria

`grep -c 'sdd-ruling' plugin/skills/_shared/console-on-pr.md plugin/skills/wrap-up/console-execution.md plugin/skills/flow/multispec-review-console.md` prints at least `1` for each file, and each hit's surrounding text names reverse (never a bare decline) for an unticked or declined ruling row.

`grep -c 'reverse' plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console-interactive.md` prints at least `2` (the existing paragraph plus the Override option description).

The new conformance pins pass, and each fails when its prose clause is removed (prove in a scratch worktree, never `git stash`).

`npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Ratify-or-reverse for a carried-forward SDD ruling now works on the PR-hosted Review Console and in multi-spec runs, not only in the single-spec chat console.

Origin: SDD controller final-review finding on #3401 (run 2026-10-17T190411-spec-3401)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

The open-items ledger is a 5-column markdown table (`_shared/ledger-format.md`). `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/ledger-write.js`'s `flipLedgerRow` splits a row on `|` and throws "expected 5-column shape" when a cell's own text contains a pipe. `plugin/bin/wrap-up-engine.js finish-console` runs its ledger flips as step 3, after steps 1-2 (decision log + memory/upstream writes) have already completed, so a `|` inside an Item or Resolution cell fails the console's Approve-all mid-way and leaves a partially-flipped ledger for the operator to reconcile. Until #3401 no SDD-carried row was flipped mechanically; #3401 now appends `SDD ruling — {one-liner}` rows whose text is copied from `progress.md` `Ruling:` lines, which commonly quote regex alternations (`a|b|c`) and table fragments — so the first pipe-bearing ruling that reaches the console breaks finish-console step 3. Nothing escapes or rejects a `|` at append time today (`/claude-tweaks:ledger` Add Item, `review/step3-routing.md`'s row append, `build/dispatch.md`'s carry-forward). Found by #3401's whole-branch review (Minor, pre-existing hazard in the ledger code, surfaced by the new producer).

## Deliverables

Pick one mechanism and apply it at every ledger-row writer: escape `|` as `\|` on append (markdown-table-safe) and unescape on read in `bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js`'s `parseLedger` and `ledger-write.js`'s `flipLedgerRow`, OR reject a pipe-bearing cell at append time with a stated substitution rule (e.g. `∣` U+2223). State the chosen rule once in `_shared/ledger-format.md`'s Format section.

`flipLedgerRow` tolerates an escaped pipe inside a cell (no longer throws on a 5-column row whose cell text carries `\|`).

`build/dispatch.md`'s carry-forward and `review/step3-routing.md`'s append cite the rule rather than restating it.

Tests: `tests/bin-lib/wrap-up/ledger-write.test.js` (or the suite that owns `flipLedgerRow`) gains a case flipping a row whose Item text carries a pipe, plus a round-trip through `parseLedger`; a `finish-console` test with such a row in the payload completes all three steps.

## Acceptance Criteria

A ledger row whose Item cell contains `a|b` (written through the chosen rule) is flipped by `wrap-up-engine.js finish-console --approve-all` without a step-3 failure, and `parseLedger` reads it back as 5 columns with the original text.

`node --test` on the owning suites passes, and the new pipe case fails against the pre-change `ledger-write.js` (prove via `git show HEAD:...` to a temp path, never `git stash`).

`npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

A ledger item whose text contains a vertical bar no longer breaks the wrap-up Review Console's Approve-all midway.

# Reflect — staged finding 3

**Category:** tangential

Origin: reflect full from #3401

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`bin/verify.js` refuses `--scope <decl> --integration-branch <ref>` together with `--baseline <ref> --baseline-cmd <name>=…`: the baseline flag requires a declared `--cmd`, and the scoped form (map-shaped `checks.tests`) declares none, so the call exits 2 with `--baseline-cmd "tests" names no declared --cmd (declared: none)`. `test/verification.md`'s Re-verify scoping table sends `/flow`'s test phase and every re-verify site down the scoped form, while its Baseline adjudication section is reachable only from the explicit `--cmd` form.

On run `2026-10-17T190411-spec-3401` (host load average 229, three sibling runs) the scoped test-phase run failed on two timing assertions in `flaky.files`, the one allowed retry also failed, and the only way to adjudicate against the base was to abandon the scoped form and re-launch the explicit full form with `--baseline origin/main` — a second ~10-minute full run whose scope the declaration had already resolved to `full` anyway. Refs #3401.

## Deliverables

`bin/verify.js` accepts `--baseline <ref>` alongside `--scope`: when the declaration maps suites, `--baseline-cmd` may name a declared suite (`tests`, `journeys`, …) or be omitted in favour of the declaration's `retry` template for that suite, which already carries the `{file}` placeholder the baseline run needs.

`test/verification.md`'s Re-verify scoping table states that a scoped site passes `--baseline {ref}` on the same invocation, and its Baseline adjudication section names the map-form resolution rule; `flow/steps-and-gates.md`'s test-gate row cites it rather than restating it.

`tests/bin-lib/verify/cli.test.js` pins the combined invocation (scoped + baseline) parsing cleanly and a usage error only when a named `--baseline-cmd` matches neither a `--cmd` nor a declared suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

`node plugin/bin/verify.js --scope .claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json --integration-branch main --baseline origin/main --no-stamp` exits 0 or 1 on a fixture repo — never 2 — and `report.json` carries both `scope` and `baselineAdjudicated` fields.

`node --test tests/bin-lib/verify/cli.test.js` passes and the new combined-invocation test fails when the exit-2 guard is restored.

`npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Verification: a scoped re-verify can now adjudicate failures against the integration branch in the same run, instead of forcing a second full suite under host load.

_Filed by `reflect` via specShapedBody._

# Reflect — staged finding 1

**Category:** tangential

Origin: reflect hindsight from #3401

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md` line 14 carries two "append a ledger row, then stage a file, then log STAGED" procedures that an LLM controller performs by hand: the `build-deviation-{N}` staging and, since #3401, the SDD `Ruling:` carry-forward. Each is a three-step prose dance whose coupling is the ledger item number the staged file's `Ledger:` header must name — so the row is appended first, the file second, and the row's Item text is rewritten afterwards when `stage-item.js --allocate` renumbers the id.

#3401's own review found five failure-branch gaps in that prose in a single pass (run ledger `docs/plans/2026-10-17-sdd-ruling-console-ledger.md` rows 20-24: no `stage-item.js` failure branch, an unsanctioned Item-cell rewrite, De-duplication on Append swallowing a second ruling, a reverse write-back ordered before the record number existed, an empty-resolution path `finish-console` rejects). Every one of them is a step a mechanical writer would not have been able to skip. Refs #3401.

## Deliverables

A `--ledger <path>` mode on `plugin/bin/stage-item.js` (or a sibling `bin/carry-forward.js`) that, in one call: appends the ledger row through `bin/lib/wrap-up/ledger-write.js`'s table parser (never De-duplication on Append), allocates the staged id, writes the staged file with `Ledger: {path}#{item}` already filled, prints the actual path, and logs the `STAGED` line via `bin/lib/log-decision/append.js`'s `formatEntry`; on any failure after the append it strips the `(staged/…)` suffix from the row it wrote and logs the Degrade-trace `SKIP` line itself.

`dispatch.md`'s `build-deviation-{N}` and `sdd-ruling-{N}` prose each collapse to one CLI invocation plus the one-liner they pass; the hand-performed ordering, renumbering, failure, and dedupe clauses added by #3401 and its review are deleted, not kept beside the CLI.

Conformance pins in `tests/build-sdd-ledger-residue-carryforward.test.js` and the build-deviation suite point at the CLI call; a CLI test proves the failure branch leaves the row `open` without a staged suffix.

## Acceptance Criteria

`grep -c "stage-item.js" plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md` prints at least `2` and `grep -c "update the just-appended row" plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md` prints `0`.

A CLI test appends a ruling row to a fixture ledger, stages `sdd-ruling-1.md`, and asserts the staged file's `Ledger:` header names the appended item number and the row's Item cell names the path the CLI actually wrote; a second test forces the write to fail and asserts the row is `open` with no `(staged/` substring and a `SKIP … (degraded): condition:` line was logged.

`npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Build: SDD ruling and build-deviation carry-forwards now stage through one CLI call, so a failed staging can no longer leave a ledger row pointing at a file that was never written.

_Filed by `reflect` via specShapedBody._

Origin: #2964 open-items ledger row 1 (docs/plans/2026-10-18-capture-argument-hint-producer-flags-ledger.md), merged in PR #3487; the SDD controller deliberately scoped the migration out of #2964 (ledger row 9).

Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

## Current State

PR #3487 (record #2964) recorded the argument-hint rule in `docs/skill-authoring.md` permissively: a flag only a producer skill or an agent passes MAY be left out of `argument-hint` when its `## Input` row is marked `(producer-only)`, and `tests/argument-hint-input.test.js`'s `undocumentedHintFlags` check exempts marked rows. `capture` and `routine` follow it.

Five skills still carry caller-only flags in their hints: `visual-review`, `design-wrapper` and `visualize` (`--source`), `tidy` (`--source sweep`) and `specify` (`--source sweep`, `--chained`). Their `## Input` rows are unmarked, so the corpus states the rule two ways, and nothing checks the inverse direction (a marked row must not appear in the hint).

## Deliverables

- Remove the caller-only flags from the five skills' `argument-hint` frontmatter and from every mirror surface that restates the hint (`plugin/skills/help/reference-card.md` and any other listing `tests/argument-hint-input.test.js` already pins), and mark the corresponding `## Input` rows `(producer-only)`.

- Tighten the rule in `docs/skill-authoring.md` (and its restatement in `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md`) from "may be left out" to "stays out".

- Add the inverse check to `tests/argument-hint-input.test.js`: a `(producer-only)` row's flag must not appear in that skill's hint, asserted per skill across the corpus.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: no `argument-hint` line in `plugin/skills/*/SKILL.md` contains `--source`, `--source sweep`, or `--chained`.

- AC2: `node --test tests/argument-hint-input.test.js` passes, and reverting one hint migration (re-adding `--source` to `visualize`'s hint) makes the new inverse check red naming that skill.

- AC3: `docs/skill-authoring.md` states the producer-only flag stays out of the hint; the permissive "may be left out" wording is gone from both it and `plan-authoring-checks.md`.

## Release Note

Skill argument hints list only the flags a person types; producer-only flags live in each skill's Input table.

groups.body:
**Related:** #3412, #3416, #3249, #3311

Origin: dispatch close-out of PR #3439 (#3412), 2026-10-18

Defer-reason: pre-existing-outside-diff

## Current State

- A multi-record `/flow` run can have its PR merged while one of its records is still being built. On 2026-10-17, PR #3348 (run `2026-10-17T062549-spec-3307-3308-3306-3309-3310-3311`) was squash-merged at 18:33Z, on explicit human instruction, closing #3306-#3310 only; its body's `Fixes #3311` had been changed to `Refs #3311`. #3311 was still mid-build in the run's locked worktree `skill-size-limits-3230`.
- About two minutes later (18:35:05Z) the reconciler closed and archived the whole run: its archived `run-state.json` reads `status: clean`, `worktree: null`, and the directory moved to `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/archive/`. The owning session's #3311 work (full build plus a review fix wave) was still unpushed at that point.
- #3412 (merged as 5cf9073d3, PR #3439) fixed the claim half: `release-merged.js` now releases only claims whose issue the merged PR actually closes. It did not touch `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`.
- On main, every merged-PR archive path in `archive-merged.js` keys only on the PR being MERGED plus console/staged state: `decideArchiveCore` (archive once MERGED and the console is resolved, or `console: none` with nothing pending in `staged/`, #3249), and the by-number fallback in the main loop (the same rule via `resolvePrStateByNumber`). Neither checks whether the merged PR closed every record in the run's `manifest.yml`, so a partially-shipped run is treated as finished.
- #3416 is a different trigger with the same symptom: a reused branch name resolves to an earlier merged PR, so a run whose own PR is still open gets archived.

## Deliverables

- Before archiving a run on merged-PR evidence, check that the merged PR closes every record the run claims: the manifest's spec ids for a multi-record run, or the single record for a singleton. Use the closing-issue data #3412 added to `pr-state.js` (`closingIssuesReferences`). When any record is not closed, skip archival with a distinct tracked reason (e.g. `merged-partial`) and leave `run-state.json` untouched (no `status: clean`, no `worktree: null`).
- Apply the same check on every merged-PR archive path in `archive-merged.js`: the branch-joined path through `decideArchiveCore`, and the by-number fallback.
- Keep #3249's behaviour for a merged run whose PR closes all of its records: it still archives with no manual step.

### Technical Approach

Read the run's record set from `manifest.yml` (`multispec.specs[].id`), falling back to the run's single record id for a singleton. Pass the merged PR's closing-issue numbers (from `pr-state.js`, extended by #3412) into the archive decision, and make it return `skip` with a `merged-partial` reason when the set difference is non-empty. Keep `decideArchiveCore` pure by having the caller supply both sets. Decide whether `merged-partial` belongs in `STRUCTURALLY_STUCK_REASONS` (escalate) or should wait for a later PR; it should not freeze silently.

#### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js` — `decideArchiveCore` and the by-number fallback: add the all-records-closed check
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/pr-state.js` — reuse the closing-issue data #3412 added; extend the by-number read if it lacks it
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js` — partial-merge, full-merge and singleton cases

### Gotchas

- Coordinate with #3416, which changes how the run's PR is resolved in the same main loop. Land whichever goes second on top of the other's PR lookup.
- A run legitimately split across two PRs will now wait for the second PR before it archives. That is intended, but the skip reason has to make it visible rather than looking stuck.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A run whose PR is MERGED but whose manifest lists a record the PR does not close is not archived. Its `run-state.json` keeps its status and worktree, and the skip reason names the unclosed record(s).
- [ ] A run whose PR is MERGED and closes every manifest record still archives exactly as today, on both the branch-joined and by-number paths.
- [ ] A singleton run (no multi-record manifest) behaves as today when its PR closes its record.
- [ ] When closing-issue data cannot be read (gh failure), archival is skipped with a transport reason, never assumed complete.
- [ ] A regression test reproduces the partial-merge archive and fails on the pre-fix code.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fix the reconciler archiving a pipeline run whose PR merged before all of its records were built.

_Filed by `capture` via specShapedBody._

Origin: reflect full from #3417

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

Two lexical containment primitives now coexist under `plugin/bin/`. `shared-primitives.js`'s `isPathContained(candidate, root, { orEqual })` is a bare `candidate.startsWith(root + path.sep)`; `plugin/bin/lib/path-guard`'s `isAncestorOrSelf(ancestor, candidate, { pathImpl })` (added by #3417) uses `path.relative`, admits equality, tests the `..` path segment (so a child named `..foo` is contained), and takes a `pathImpl` so win32 compares case-insensitively and across drives.

`isPathContained` still has six production callers outside `shared-primitives.js`: `skill-load-report.js`, `load-delta.js`, `lib/init/release-bootstrap.js`, `lib/reconcile/reap-merged.js`, `lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js` and `lib/hooks/worktree-reap.js`. #3417 migrated `timing/transcript.js` and `installed-plugins.js` to the path-guard form and left these alone because the spec scoped three call sites. `.claude/skills/pre-tool-use-gate-exemptions/SKILL.md` and `docs/donts.md` [IL-161] now point authors at different helpers for the same question.

## Deliverables

- Decide the single lexical containment primitive. Either `isPathContained` delegates to `path-guard`'s `isAncestorOrSelf` (keeping its `orEqual` option as a thin wrapper), or its callers migrate and it is removed.

- Migrate the remaining `isPathContained` callers, each with its existing suite unmodified, and record any caller whose behavior intentionally changes (a `..foo` child, win32 case-insensitivity) the way #3417 recorded its two.

- Update `.claude/skills/pre-tool-use-gate-exemptions/SKILL.md`'s containment bullet and `docs/donts.md` [IL-161] to name the one surviving helper.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -rn "startsWith(.*path.sep)" plugin/bin` shows no hand-rolled containment test, and `isPathContained` and `isAncestorOrSelf` no longer both exist as independent implementations.

- [ ] Every migrated caller's existing test suite passes unmodified, and a characterization case pins each intended behavior change.

- [ ] `docs/donts.md` [IL-161] and the `pre-tool-use-gate-exemptions` skill name the same helper.

## Release Note

Internal hardening: plugin path-containment checks share one implementation.

`stripComments` in `tests/windows-hide-spawn-conformance.test.js` runs two regexes in sequence: block comments first, then line comments. Origin: reflect full from #3412

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`docs/plugin-structure.md:67` states that wall-clock timing budgets live in `perf/` (run by `npm run test:perf`) and never in the default `npm test` suite, because they flake under sibling-suite load. Nothing enforces that convention: #3412's build landed a `performance.now()` `< 200ms` assertion in `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/release-merged.test.js` to prove regex linearity, and it reached review before anyone noticed (open-items ledger row 23; the removal is `staged/review-1.patch` in run `2026-10-17T192303-spec-3412`). The same run hit two unrelated timing-test flakes under a load average above 200, which is the exact failure the convention exists to prevent.

Evidence: `grep -rl performance.now tests/` returns only the #3412 test file today, so the convention has held by habit alone; the repo already pins prose conventions with conformance tests (`tests/*-conformance.test.js`), so the enforcement shape exists.

Cost this session: one review finding, one staged patch, one Review Console row; no rework.

## Deliverables

A conformance test under `tests/` that scans every `tests/**/*.test.js` for a wall-clock assertion shape (`performance.now()`, `Date.now()`, or `process.hrtime` compared against a numeric budget in the same test body) and fails naming the file and line.

The test cites `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s perf/ rule in its failure message so the fix direction (move the budget to `perf/`) is on the failing line.

An allow-list mechanism for a deliberate exception, with a required one-line reason, so the gate can be bypassed visibly rather than by deleting the test.

## Acceptance Criteria

Adding a `performance.now()` budget assertion to any file under `tests/` makes `npm test` fail with the offending `file:line` and the perf/ pointer.

A budget assertion under `perf/` does not trip the test.

The existing suite passes with the test in place (zero current offenders once `staged/review-1.patch` from #3412 lands, or the one offender it names is the #3412 test and the patch is applied first).

## Release Note

Test suite: a conformance check fails any wall-clock timing budget placed under `tests/` and points at `perf/`, so timing budgets can no longer flake the default `npm test` run.

Origin: wrap-up of #3298

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

When the Review Console resolves the merge half to **leave-open** (`pending-review`), `wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md`'s phase-exit push ships the branch and the run ends. Nothing re-reads the PR's `mergeStateStatus` after that push. On #3298's run the pushed head `eb759e308` was `DIRTY` against `main` (three commits had landed since the fork, one touching the same journey Origin list), so GitHub suppressed the `test` workflow entirely (#3298 wrap-up, `decisions.md` 23:42:18) — the parked PR showed one green label job and no test run, which a human reading the PR would mistake for "checks still pending".

`_shared/pr-first-merge.md` Step 2.5's merge-verification gate reads this state, but only on the merge path. The parked path has no equivalent, so a conflict introduced by a sibling merge during the run is discovered only when a human opens the PR later.

## Deliverables

- [ ] After the wrap-up phase-exit push under `integration-model: pr-first` with a leave-open outcome, read `gh pr view {n} --json mergeStateStatus` once (via `pack.pr`'s shape); on `DIRTY`, merge `origin/{integration-branch}` into the branch in the worktree, resolve nothing automatically beyond git's own auto-merge, and push again — a real content conflict stays `DIRTY` and is reported, never silently left.
- [ ] Log the outcome to `decisions.md` (`AUTO … mergeability: {CLEAN|BLOCKED|DIRTY → merged main as {sha}|DIRTY — conflict in {files}}`) and name it in the phase-trace report's Verdict line and the flow summary's resume-to-merge row, so a parked PR with a suppressed test run is visible from the summary.
- [ ] A conformance test pins the new paragraph in `execution-and-verification.md` and `flow/summary-template.md`'s resume row wording.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `pr-first` run whose console resolves leave-open and whose PR reads `DIRTY` after the phase-exit push ends with a merge-from-main commit pushed (when git auto-merges cleanly) and a `decisions.md` line naming the merge sha; the flow summary's resume-to-merge row names the merge.
- A run whose PR reads `DIRTY` with a genuine content conflict ends with a `decisions.md` line naming the conflicting file(s) and the Verdict line reads `blocked — conflict with main in {files}`, never "everything shipped".
- A `CLEAN`/`BLOCKED`/`UNKNOWN` read changes nothing beyond the one log line.

## Release Note

A parked pr-first run now notices when a sibling merge made its PR conflict with main, merges main when git can, and says so instead of leaving a PR whose CI never ran.

Origin: ledger resolve gate (from #3204 wrap-up)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

After #3204, `unattributedFailureCount` (`plugin/bin/lib/verify/extract.js`) returns `null` for every output family other than spec/TAP, and `planRetry` (`plugin/bin/lib/verify/flaky.js`) refuses with `no-accounting-guard: {family}`. Runner-owned flaky retry therefore never fires for a jest, vitest or pytest suite; those failures route to the whole-suite re-run path in `plugin/skills/test/verification.md`.

#3204 chose refusal over an accounting check because no single cross-check fits every summary dialect: jest prints `FAIL` lines per test file while its `Tests:` totals count individual tests, and pytest collection `ERROR`s and vitest `Unhandled Errors` sit outside any `FAIL`/`FAILED` line, so a count comparison could report a log as fully accounted while a failure is not.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Add per-dialect accounting for jest (the `FAIL` file lines against `Test Suites: N failed`) and for vitest (`Test Files N failed` plus a check for an `Errors` block), so `unattributedFailureCount` returns `0` or a positive count for them instead of `null`.

- [ ] Keep pytest refusing with `no-accounting-guard: summary` unless a sound check exists: collection `ERROR`s sit outside every `FAILED` line.

- [ ] Tests with a captured log per dialect, each with an all-attributed case and an unattributed-failure case.

- [ ] Update `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` (Flake handling), `docs/journeys/run-a-deterministic-verification-check.md` Step 10, and `.claude/skills/node-test-output-evidence/SKILL.md` to match.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A jest log whose every failing file is allowlisted and fully attributed retries those files.

- [ ] A jest or vitest log carrying a failure no named file accounts for refuses with `unattributed-failures: {N}`.

- [ ] A pytest log still refuses with `no-accounting-guard: summary`.

Origin: reflect full from #3298

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/verify/changed-files.js` reads every git path list with `-z` and `--end-of-options` (lines 138, 179, 187) and documents why: without `-z`, `core.quotepath` C-quotes any non-ASCII path (`"docs/caf\303\251.md"`), so a newline-split reader sees a path that matches nothing; without `--end-of-options`, a dash-leading ref or range is parsed as a git option.

#3298's composer repeated the newline-split pattern for `git diff --name-only` and review had to add both flags after the fact (`0e23a2f09`). Five sibling readers in the plugin still split git path output on newlines with neither flag:

- `plugin/bin/lib/merge-size-probe.js:46` — `git diff --no-renames --name-only {integration}...{head}`
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/facts.js:173` and `:176` — `git diff --name-only {base}...HEAD` and `git diff --diff-filter=RD --name-status {base}...HEAD`
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js:623` — `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r {sha}`
- `plugin/bin/lib/release-preflight/pack.js:233` — `git ls-tree --name-only {tipRef}`, `.split('\n')`
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js:330` — `git diff --cached --name-status`

No `_shared` contract states the discipline, so each new reader re-derives it or misses it (`gh-api-module-pattern` covers `gh` calls, not git path reads).

## Deliverables

- [ ] Each of the five readers above passes `-z` and splits on NUL (`--name-status -z` readers parse the status/path records accordingly), and passes `--end-of-options` before any ref, range, or sha argument.
- [ ] One contract paragraph — in the `_shared` file that owns git-invocation conventions, or a new short `_shared/git-path-read.md` cited from it — states the rule: a git path-list read uses `-z` + NUL split and `--end-of-options`; `changed-files.js` and `compose-subject.js` are the reference implementations.
- [ ] A conformance test greps `plugin/bin/**/*.js` for `--name-only`/`--name-status` git argv arrays and fails on any that lacks `-z`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture repository with a path `docs/café.md` changed on the branch: `merge-size-probe.js`, `wrap-up/facts.js`'s blast-radius probe, and `pre-tool-use.js`'s staged-file read each report that path unquoted (`docs/café.md`), never `"docs/caf\303\251.md"`.
- `grep -rn -- "--name-only\|--name-status" plugin/bin --include='*.js'` lists no git argv array without `-z` on the same line, and the conformance test goes red when `-z` is removed from any one of them (revert to confirm).
- `git grep -n -- "-z" plugin/skills/_shared/` finds the contract paragraph, and it names `changed-files.js` as the reference implementation.

## Release Note

Every plugin git path-list reader now handles non-ASCII paths and dash-leading refs the same way — no silent mis-scope on a C-quoted path.

_Filed by `reflect` via specShapedBody._

Origin: #3309 final whole-branch review (ledger row 36)

Defer-reason: out-of-scope

## Current State

#3309 ships `plugin/bin/skill-load-report.js` and harness-health's Skill-load check. The check files a `by:harness-health` record when a skill's measured per-invocation load exceeds its static closure from `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/load.js` (`overClosure = max > closure`, the spec's literal contract). On real data that comparison cannot fire, for two reasons:
- Every plugin skill's closure is transitive and runs 1.20–1.96 MB (even `claude-tweaks:capture` is 1.96 MB, out of a ~5.95 MB corpus). The largest measured max over 20 sessions plus 510 subagent transcripts is 236,519 B, a ratio of 0.01–0.13.
- harness-health invokes the CLI with only `--plugin-root "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"`, so project-local `.claude/skills` always get `closure: null`. That is the only place over-closure actually showed up when the reviewer passed `.claude` explicitly (`node-test-output-evidence`, max 52,872 B against closure 15,187 B).

The spec's stated purpose is to find skills whose sessions read prose their citations never reach. `readSkillLoads` already records each invocation's `readPaths`, but the CLI discards them after summing bytes.

## Deliverables

- In `skill-load-report.js`, compare each invocation's skill-file `readPaths` against the matching entry's closure `files` (from `entryPointLoads`, normalized to the same path form). Report per skill the count and list of read files outside the closure (`outsideClosure`). Make that the filing trigger, replacing or alongside `max > closure`.
- Decide how project-local roots reach the harness-health command. One option is passing `--plugin-root .claude` when `.claude/skills/` exists. A root with no `skills/` makes the CLI exit 2 today, so the command needs a guard.
- Update harness-health's Skill-load check paragraph and its prose-pin test to match.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A fixture invocation that reads a skill file outside its closure's `files` is reported with that path in `outsideClosure` and triggers filing. Reading only closure files does not.
2. On this repo's real transcripts, the report names at least one skill with `outsideClosure` non-empty, or the PR states why none exists.
3. A project-local skill invoked from a worktree joins its `.claude/skills` closure under the harness-health command as written.

## Release Note

Health checks now flag skills whose sessions read skill files their own instructions never point to.

Origin: #3310 whole-branch review (final review Minor 5)

Defer-reason: out-of-scope

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/checks.js`'s `headroomCheck` measures each governed `.md` file with the raw `fs.statSync(abs).size`, which counts `when:` marker lines and CRLF line endings. Since #3310 it compares that raw figure to `RAIL_BYTES` (52,500 B).

The Read rail measures differently. `rail.js`'s `skillFileRailViolations` goes through `context-cost.js`'s `measureSkills`/`measureSubFiles`, which strip marker lines and normalize CRLF to LF. `plugin/skills/build/plan-audit.md` now says the rail strips only the marker lines.

Raw bytes are always greater than or equal to measured bytes, so plan-audit never misses a breach. The cost is a false positive: a marker-heavy file, or any file in a Windows CRLF checkout, sitting slightly over `RAIL_BYTES` raw gets a blocking plan-audit stop that the `rail:` tests would pass. The raw basis predates #3310; #3310 only retargeted the number.

## Deliverables

- `headroomCheck` measures per-file bytes through `context-cost.js`'s marker-stripped, CRLF-normalized measurement, the same function the rail uses. It reuses that function rather than re-implementing the stripping.
- `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/checks.test.js` gains a fixture that is over `RAIL_BYTES` raw but under it once marker lines are stripped. That fixture reports no breach. A CRLF variant does the same.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A governed fixture file whose raw size is `RAIL_BYTES + 100`, carrying more than 100 B of `<!-- when: … -->` marker lines, reports no `breaches` entry.
2. The same file with its marker lines removed, and its body padded so it stays over `RAIL_BYTES`, still reports a breach.
3. A CRLF copy of a file at exactly `RAIL_BYTES` LF bytes reports no breach.
4. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Plan audits measure a skill file's size the same way the Read-limit check does, so marker lines and Windows line endings no longer trigger a false stop.

Origin: #3309 build, Task 0 premise probe (ledger row 37)

Defer-reason: out-of-scope

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/timing/transcript.js` `locateTranscripts({ cwd, sessionId, homeDir = os.homedir(), fsImpl })` always looks under `path.join(homeDir, '.claude', 'projects')`. `plugin/bin/phase-timing.js:159` calls it with only `{ cwd: worktree, sessionId }`.

Claude Code writes transcripts to `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/` when that variable is set. `plugin/bin/dream-scan.js:66` already resolves `process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR || path.join(os.homedir(), '.claude')`, and so does #3309's `skill-load-report.js`. On a machine running Claude Code with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-accounts/<slug>`, `~/.claude/projects` holds none of the sessions, so `phase-timing.js` silently finds no transcript and reports no token or procedure-byte data.

#3309 could not fix this: its spec lists `timing/transcript.js` as "not modified".

## Deliverables

- Resolve the projects root from `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (falling back to `~/.claude`) in `locateTranscripts`, or in its caller with an injectable config-dir parameter. Keep the existing `homeDir` seam working for tests.
- Update `TRANSCRIPT_SLUG_RULE`'s header note to name the config-dir resolution.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set to a temp dir holding `projects/{slug}/{sid}.jsonl`, `locateTranscripts({ cwd, sessionId })` returns that file.
2. With `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` unset, behavior is unchanged (`tests/bin-lib/timing/transcript.test.js` passes).

- `extractCitations` resolves `skills/build/SKILL.md` and `wrap-up/cleanup-procedures.md` from a fixture SKILL.md to their real paths.
- On this repo, `plugin:flow`'s unresolved-pair count drops from 982 to the count that genuinely names nothing (stated in the PR).

Origin: reflect full from #3404

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/friction-events.js`'s `computeClaimBoundary` (#2989) reads the first `decisions.md` entry's `HH:MM:SS` and builds `new Date(`${mintDay}T${hh}:${mm}:${ss}Z`)` — it interprets the time as UTC.

`plugin/bin/lib/log-decision/append.js`'s `hms()` writes that time with `getHours()/getMinutes()/getSeconds()` — local time. `events.jsonl` timestamps are ISO UTC.

On any machine east of UTC the computed claim boundary lands hours after the run's real events, so `readEvents` drops every event as "pre-claim noise". Observed on #3404's run (UTC+2): `events.jsonl` held 5 `wd-guard-refusal` events, yet `node bin/friction-events.js --run <run-dir>` printed `[]`, so `/reflect`'s Friction lens saw a frictionless run.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Make `computeClaimBoundary` read the `decisions.md` time as local time, matching `hms()`, so the boundary is the same instant the entry was written.

- [ ] Add a regression test that runs the boundary computation under a non-UTC `TZ` (for example `Europe/Copenhagen`) and asserts events after the first claim entry survive while earlier unrelated events are still dropped.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Under `TZ=Europe/Copenhagen`, a run dir whose `decisions.md` first entry reads `20:39:18` and whose `events.jsonl` holds events at `2026-10-17T18:40:00Z` returns those events from `friction-events.js`.

- The existing #2989 tests (pre-claim events still dropped) pass unchanged, and a new test fails with the old `Z` construction (revert to confirm).

## Release Note

Fixes the Friction lens silently reporting a frictionless run for operators east of UTC.

Origin: reflect light from #3389

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/wrap-up-engine.js plan` gathers its repo facts (changed files, renamed/deleted paths, journey frontmatter overlap, CLAUDE.md budget) through `resolveRepoRoot()`, which runs `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` and takes its dirname. From a linked worktree that is the MAIN checkout, not the worktree the run is building in, so `git diff {base}...HEAD` runs against the main checkout's HEAD. Observed on run 2026-10-17T183731-record-3389 (worktree `dispatch-record-3389`, a 6-file diff touching `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js`): `gatherFacts` with `cwd` = the worktree returns 6 changed files including `resolve.js`; with `cwd` = the common-dir root it returns 0, and `plan` printed the journeys row with `candidates: []` even though `docs/journeys/resolve-the-unattended-console-in-one-process-1932.md` lists `resolve.js` in its `files:` frontmatter.

The common-dir resolution is deliberate for telemetry (`resolveTelemetryPath` anchors `.claude-tweaks/wrap-up-outcomes.tsv` to the main checkout) and was reused for facts by #3017 to fix the subdirectory-cwd case. The facts read needs the worktree top-level instead. `runVerifyVerb` (around line 517) also calls `resolveRepoRoot`; its `--base` diff has the same exposure. Gates that fall out of the wrong diff (CLAUDE.md Commands renamed, renamed/deleted references, journey overlap) can silently close in worktree runs, which is every `/flow` run.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Resolve a second root for repo facts: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the invocation cwd (the worktree top-level inside a linked worktree, the checkout root otherwise, the subdirectory case still handled). Keep `resolveRepoRoot` (common-dir) only for the telemetry path.

- [ ] Use the top-level for `gatherFacts` and `buildJourneyFrontmatter` in `runPlan`, and audit `runVerifyVerb`'s use for the same exposure.

- [ ] Add a regression test under `tests/` that builds a linked worktree fixture with a changed file named in a journey's `files:` frontmatter and asserts `plan`'s journeys row carries that journey as a candidate (it must fail against the common-dir resolution).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wrap-up-engine.js plan` run from a linked worktree reports the worktree branch's own changed files, so a journey whose `files:` overlaps the diff appears in the journeys row's `scope.candidates`.

- Telemetry still lands in the main checkout's `.claude-tweaks/wrap-up-outcomes.tsv`.

- The new test goes red when `runPlan` is pointed back at the common-dir root.

## Release Note

Wrap-up's curation plan now reads the branch diff from the worktree it runs in, so journey, reference and CLAUDE.md gates no longer close on an empty diff in worktree runs.

groups.body:
Surface: backend

## Overview

Part of the "Build dispatch cost shape" decomposition (origin #3229, a feedback report from a measured 10-task subagent-driven build). In that build, 3 of the 5 Important findings from the top-tier final review were spec or plan-level gaps — behaviour the spec left undecided, or two tasks disagreeing about a contract — found after all the code was written and fixed in an 18-minute fix wave plus a re-review. SDD's own pre-flight scan ("Before dispatching Task 1, scan the plan once for conflicts") runs on the controller and hunts contradictions between and within tasks; it does not look for spec gaps or undecided behaviour.

This record adds a new `/build` Common Step between plan audit (Common Step 1.5) and execution dispatch (Common Step 2), Spec Mode only: one dispatched reviewer on the Capable profile reads the materialized spec and the plan once and returns findings in three classes — spec gap (the spec does not decide something the plan must decide), undecided behaviour (an input class, failure mode or UI state no task covers) and cross-task contract (one task produces what another consumes and they disagree). It explicitly does not redo SDD's pre-flight conflict table. A spec gap resolvable from the spec's own intent amends the in-run materialized spec before Task 1; a spec gap that needs a human becomes a deliberate new HARD-GATE stop; the other two classes amend the plan.

**Complexity:** Medium-High
**Estimated tasks:** 6-8

## Non-Goals

- Redoing SDD's pre-flight conflict table (cross-task and within-task contradictions, written to the SDD ledger). The reviewer's brief tells it to skip that class.
- Editing the live issue body at any point. An intent-resolvable spec amendment lives in the worktree's materialized spec and is posted once as a comment on the record; nothing is staged for the Review Console.
- Running in design mode (no materialized spec, no record) — same skip as architecture alignment.
- Changing SDD's per-task loop, or filing anything upstream with superpowers.
- The per-task tier markers (a separate record, which adds one check to this record's reviewer once both exist).

## Prerequisites

| Record | Title | Status |
|--------|-------|--------|
| #3375 | Attribute agent cost to individual subagent dispatches in phase-timing and the /wrap-up run summary | must ship first, so the plan reviewer's own cost and the final-review finding classes it is meant to reduce are measurable |
| #3376 | Re-pin superpowers to 7.0.0 and pin the upstream text the dispatch cost-shape changes lean on | must ship first, so the SDD pre-flight sentence this step is defined against is pinned |
| #3310 | Cut every skill-size consumer over to the rail, load delta, and size outlier | ready, in progress — shares `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md`, `plan-audit.md`, `plan-authoring-checks.md`, `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/checks.js`; build after it merges |

## Current State

- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` — `### Common Step 1.5: Plan Audit`, then `### Common Step 1.7: Design Pre-Build (frontend specs + terminal)`, then `### Common Step 2: Execute the Plan`. The file is 45,995 bytes against the shared 51,200-byte ceiling, so the new step must be a short pointer to a new sub-file (measured 2026-10-17).
- `plugin/skills/build/plan-audit.md` and `plugin/bin/plan-audit.js` — the mechanical plan audit (Checks A-E plus headroom) that Step 1.5 runs; Check E (warn-only) already compares the materialized spec's Acceptance Criteria clauses to the plan.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` — the dispatch contract (minimal input, trailing `STATUS:` line, inlined output template, model profile selection); Template A (a findings table) lives in `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-dispatch-core.md`'s Template A section.
- `plugin/bin/resolve-profile.js` — resolves `capable` to a model; dispatch sites call it and pass the model explicitly.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-decision-log.md` — the canonical entry schema for `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/{run-id}/decisions.md`.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md` — the "What `auto` never silences" table; its HARD-GATE / BLOCKED / STOP row (around line 208) names `/build` Design Step 3 plan validation and Common Step 1.5 plan-audit hard-fails, and has no entry for a step between 1.5 and 2.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/ceremony-profile.md` — the single roster of what each `ceremony-profile` skips, pinned by `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js`.
- `plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md` — the materialized spec (`work/{n}-spec.md`) lives in the worktree's copy in worktree mode, not under `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`, and reaches the main checkout only on merge.
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` — how `/dispatch` blocks a record today: a `gh issue comment` attempt comment, then `bot:blocked` added (and every `auto:*` grant removed) with a `PushNotification`. `plugin/skills/_shared/headless-self-report.md` and `DISPATCH_HEADLESS=1` are the existing "no human present" signals.
- `docs/skill-graph.md` — the `## build` section is where any new `/build` edge is stated, once.

## Deliverables

- [ ] A new sub-file in `plugin/skills/build/` (the builder names it; `plan-review.md` suggested) holding the full procedure: skip conditions, the dispatch prompt with the inlined output template, the three finding classes, and the per-class handling below.
- [ ] A short new Common Step in `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` between 1.5 and 2 that states the Spec-Mode-only condition and points at the sub-file (pointer only; no procedure restated in `SKILL.md`).
- [ ] The dispatch: one reviewer on Capable, model resolved through `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/resolve-profile.js" capable --run-dir "$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR"`, under the Subagent Contract. Input is the materialized spec path and plan path only (no conversation history); the reviewer may also read the repository read-only to check what the plan integrates with, because undecided-behaviour and cross-task findings depend on existing code; trailing `STATUS:` line; output template inlined verbatim in the prompt.
- [ ] The output template carries, for each spec-gap finding, a `Resolution` field (`intent-resolvable` or `needs-human`) and the spec sentence that supports an `intent-resolvable` call. Burden of proof: when no spec sentence can be cited, the finding is `needs-human`. A gap is `needs-human` whenever it would alter or loosen an existing Acceptance Criterion or an observable contract, or has two defensible readings. An undecided-behaviour finding that is really a product decision is reclassified by the reviewer as a spec gap.
- [ ] The class boundary against SDD's pre-flight scan is written into the brief: the pre-flight scan checks plan-internal contradictions (a task against the plan's Global Constraints, a step the plan mandates that the review rubric forbids); this reviewer checks producer/consumer agreement between tasks (names, shapes, ordering of what one task produces and another consumes) and each against the spec. The brief gives one example of each.
- [ ] Handling for a spec gap marked `intent-resolvable`: amend the worktree's copy of `work/{n}-spec.md` before Task 1 with an additive clarification only (never editing or loosening an existing Acceptance Criterion), commit the amendment in the worktree together with any plan amendment, write the decision log entry per `_shared/auto-decision-log.md`, and post the amendment as one comment on the record (`gh issue comment`, or the MCP equivalent per `_shared/github-write-transport.md`) so the record's history carries it. The record body is never edited and nothing is staged for the Review Console: the amended in-run spec is the one `/test`, `/review` and `/wrap-up` judge against, so there is no staged item to apply, decline, or leave unreached.
- [ ] Handling for undecided-behaviour and cross-task-contract findings: amend the plan file, log it, and proceed. After any spec or plan amendment, re-run `plan-audit.js` once on the amended plan (Checks A, C, D, headroom, and E against the amended spec); the plan review itself does not re-run, so the step cannot loop.
- [ ] Standalone `/build` (no `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`, no `config.yml`): the step still runs and amends the spec; the decision-log write is skipped and the amendment is listed in the Step 7 handoff (the record comment is still posted) (the same standalone fallback `plan-audit.md` and `SKILL.md` use for their own run-directory-anchored parts).
- [ ] A new HARD-GATE row in `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md` for a spec gap marked `needs-human`: a real stop before Task 1 in every mode when someone is present; when nobody is (`DISPATCH_HEADLESS=1`, the existing headless marker `/dispatch` sets for a scheduled Routine drain), the record goes `bot:blocked` with the question posted on it, through the transport `/dispatch` already uses for blocked records (issue comment, `bot:blocked`, every `auto:*` grant removed). The row names the exit state: the claim is released, the worktree and draft PR are left in place, nothing is merged, and the run reports `BLOCKED` with the question to its caller; a human answers on the record, re-grants `auto:build` at `/claude-tweaks:backlog refine`, and the next dispatch re-materializes from the answered record.
- [ ] The same HARD-GATE enumeration is updated at every consumer that restates it: `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-card.md` (line 36 lists the same gate families) and any other file a repo-wide grep for the existing row's wording finds, with a conformance assertion that each named consumer cites the new gate.
- [ ] The skip conditions: `ceremony-profile: fast-lane` (a new roster row with a new tag in `plugin/skills/_shared/ceremony-profile.md`), and a trivial plan (the builder picks and documents the threshold, reusing an existing triviality signal such as Step 1.5's fewer-than-3-file-references condition where it fits). A skip writes a `SKIP` entry per `_shared/auto-decision-log.md`'s degrade-trace rule.
- [ ] The reviewer's brief tells it explicitly not to repeat SDD's pre-flight conflict table.
- [ ] Any new `/build` edge added to `docs/skill-graph.md`'s `## build` section (for example to `/dispatch` for the blocked-record transport).
- [ ] Tests: a conformance suite pinning the new step's placement and pointer, the roster row, and the HARD-GATE row; plus byte-ceiling checks for every grown file.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` contains a Common Step positioned after `Common Step 1.5: Plan Audit` and before `Common Step 2: Execute the Plan` that names Spec Mode only and points at the new sub-file, and the file stays under 51,200 bytes (and under any tighter per-skill pin found by the Byte-pin check).
2. The new sub-file states the three finding classes by name (spec gap, undecided behaviour, cross-task contract), states that SDD's pre-flight conflict table is not redone, and inlines the output template and a trailing `STATUS:` requirement verbatim in the dispatch prompt text.
3. The sub-file's dispatch resolves the model with `resolve-profile.js capable` and passes the resolved model explicitly; no model name is hardcoded.
4. For an `intent-resolvable` spec-gap finding the sub-file prescribes, in order: amend the worktree's `work/{n}-spec.md` additively (never editing or loosening an existing Acceptance Criterion), commit it, log the decision, post the amendment as one comment on the record, and re-run `plan-audit.js` once; and states that no `gh issue edit` runs against the live record and nothing is staged for the Review Console. The sub-file states the standalone-`/build` fallback (amendment listed in the Step 7 handoff, no decision-log write).
5. `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md`'s HARD-GATE row names this step's `needs-human` spec gap, and states the two behaviours (real stop when someone is present, in every mode; `bot:blocked` with the question posted when `DISPATCH_HEADLESS=1`), the exit state (claim released, worktree and draft PR left in place, `BLOCKED` reported to the caller) and the resume path. `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-card.md` and every other file the repo-wide grep finds cite the new gate, pinned by a conformance assertion.
6. `plugin/skills/_shared/ceremony-profile.md` gains one Skips-table row for this step with a new tag, and `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js` passes with the tag present in the citing skill text.
7. The step does not run in design mode and is skipped, with a `SKIP` decision-log entry, for a `fast-lane` run and for a plan under the documented triviality threshold.
8. `docs/skill-graph.md` states each new edge once, and no `SKILL.md` restates an edge.
9. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Added a top-tier plan review before the first build task that catches spec gaps and undecided behaviour early, and stops the build for a human decision when the spec cannot answer.

## Technical Approach

The reviewer reads two files and returns a findings table in Template A shape with an added `Class` column (spec gap / undecided behaviour / cross-task contract) so the controller routes mechanically rather than paraphrasing. The controller (the `/build` session) applies the per-class handling; the reviewer is read-only. Placement relative to Common Step 1.7 (Design Pre-Build) is the builder's call; running the plan review before 1.7 is recommended because plan amendments should land before design references are pre-loaded for implementers.

### Data / API Surface

- Output template (builder finalizes): `| Severity | Class | Resolution | Path:Line | Finding | Evidence | Suggested resolution |`, "No findings." when clean, at most 7 rows with a "+N more" row, trailing `STATUS: {WORD}` line. `Resolution` is filled only for spec-gap rows and `Evidence` must cite a spec sentence for `intent-resolvable`. Routing keys on Class and Resolution, never on Severity; `low` and `info` findings are logged only and amend nothing.
- Decision-log entries per `_shared/auto-decision-log.md`: `AUTO` for an amendment applied, `SKIP` for a skipped step. No `STAGED` entry: nothing is staged.
- Human-needed gate in headless runs: a `gh issue comment` carrying the question, then `bot:blocked` (bootstrapped per `_shared/label-bootstrap.md`) and removal of `auto:*` grants, mirroring `dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` Settle steps 5-6 but without the retry-ceiling counter (this gate blocks directly).

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/build/plan-review.md` — new file (name is the builder's call): the full procedure
- `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md` — new Common Step pointer between 1.5 and 2 (45,995 bytes now; 51,200 ceiling)
- `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md` — new HARD-GATE entry for the human-needed spec gap
- `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-card.md` — restates the HARD-GATE families (line 36); add the new gate
- `plugin/skills/_shared/ceremony-profile.md` — new Skips-table row and tag
- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` — read-only: the contract the dispatch follows
- `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-decision-log.md` — read-only: entry schema
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` — read-only: the blocked-record transport to reuse
- `plugin/bin/resolve-profile.js` — read-only: Capable resolution
- `docs/skill-graph.md` — new edge(s) in the `## build` section
- `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js` — roster pin the new row must satisfy
- `tests/build-dispatch-subfile-table-completeness.test.js` — checks `build/` sub-files are listed where required; the new file must satisfy it

## Gotchas

- Steering principle for the whole decomposition: claude-tweaks never files upstream with superpowers and never contradicts SDD's text. This step runs before SDD starts and adds a review SDD does not have; it must not instruct SDD to skip or alter its own pre-flight scan.
- The materialized spec lives in the worktree's copy of `work/{n}-spec.md` in worktree mode, not under `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR`, and reaches the main checkout only on merge (`plugin/skills/flow/materialize.md`). Amend that copy — amending a path under the run directory silently edits nothing the later phases read (`[IL-127]` shadow-copy hazard).
- Anti-goal: a plan review that rules on spec gaps in the SDD ledger only, leaving the spec that `/test`, `/review` and `/wrap-up` judge against unchanged. The amendment must land in the materialized spec.
- Anti-goal: any new mid-flow stop in `auto` mode that is not added to the auto-mode contract's HARD-GATE list deliberately. The human-needed spec gap is that deliberate addition; every other finding class resolves without a stop.
- The Capable reviewer is a dispatch the Subagent Contract governs: `Frontier` is reserved for contract-enumerated singleton slots, so this stays Capable regardless of `profile=frontier`.
- "Someone is present" means `DISPATCH_HEADLESS` is not `1`. `plugin/skills/dispatch/task-prompt.md` (First call section) has the dispatching session add `DISPATCH_HEADLESS=1` to the `/claude-tweaks:flow` invocation exactly when the firing came from a scheduled Routine drain with nobody present, and omit it when a human typed the command. Interactive `/flow` in `auto` where the user has since walked away is accepted as "present" (the stop waits for them); that is the stated cost of making this a real stop. ASSUMPTION — verify at build: a human-typed `/dispatch #N` runs the build in a Task subagent that cannot call `AskUserQuestion`, so the stop there must surface as a `BLOCKED` report that the dispatching session (where the human is) relays — via reading `dispatch/SKILL.md`'s Settle handling of a `BLOCKED` build call and `_shared/headless-self-report.md`; define that relay in this record rather than leaving a stop nobody can answer.
- ASSUMPTION — verify at build: the retry-ceiling path in Settle is not the right mechanism for this gate (a human-needed spec gap should block on the first occurrence, not after three failed attempts) — via reading `dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` steps 5-6 and `_shared/issue-claims.md`'s rule that `bot:blocked` removes all `auto:*` labels.
- The new HARD-GATE row is a contract change under the repo's expand-contract discipline: add the row, update every consumer that enumerates the HARD-GATE list, and never rename an existing gate. Known consumers at record-writing time (2026-10-17): `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-contract.md` line 208 (the row itself) and `plugin/skills/_shared/auto-mode-card.md` line 36 (restates the gate families); grep the repo for "plan-audit hard-fails" and "plan validation" to find any others, including under `plugin/skills/flow/` and `plugin/skills/dispatch/`.
- Amending the spec after the plan was written can trip `build/SKILL.md`'s plan-staleness rule on a resumed build ("has the spec evolved since the plan was written?"). Committing the spec amendment together with the plan amendment, in the same commit, is what keeps the pair consistent; say so in the sub-file.
- Decided (2026-10-17): the live record body is never edited and nothing is staged. The record comment is the durable trace on the issue; the worktree's amended spec reaches `main` only on merge. Do not add a Review Console apply path or a new staged-item kind.
- This record shares `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md`, `plan-audit.md`, `plan-authoring-checks.md` and `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/checks.js` with #3310 (ready, in progress) — build after it merges and re-read the files. Other ready records touching `build/SKILL.md` (#3118, #3079, #3060, #3004) and `build/dispatch.md` (#3118, #3004, #2869) may land first; expect rebasing, and `docs/skill-graph.md` is shared with #3033.
- Measure byte headroom before adding to `plugin/skills/build/SKILL.md`: 5,205 bytes remain. The pointer must be a few lines; everything else lives in the new sub-file.
- Trivial-plan threshold: reuse Step 1.5's existing triviality language ("fewer than 3 file references and no `Scope keywords:`") unless the builder can justify a different measure; do not invent a second definition of "trivial" without citing why.

# Reflect — staged finding 1

**Category:** tangential
Origin: reflect light from #3337

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:flow` Step 2.8 mints the run directory (`resolve-run-dir --create`) and then immediately writes the claim-log line into its `decisions.md` (`flow/claim-targets.md`, #2492), before Step 3 writes `config.yml` or any `run-state.json` exists.

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` `isUnadoptedMint` (line 54) excludes a mint from fallback event attribution only while it carries neither `run-state.json` nor `decisions.md`. Once the claim line lands, the mint is an unowned, newest, non-terminal run, so `post-tool-use.js`'s fallback attribution (`attribution: 'fallback'`) routes sibling sessions' events into its `events.jsonl`.

`plugin/bin/lib/flow/preflight.js:145` then computes `hasOtherContent = decisionsHasContent || nonEmpty(events.jsonl) || specMaterialized`, so a fresh mint with only foreign fallback events adopts as **case 3** (repair: backfill worktree, PR, materialize) instead of **case 2** (fresh). #3242 fixed the same misclassification for Step 1.5/1.8 `decisions.md` content; the `events.jsonl` arm is untouched.

Observed in run `2026-10-17T075913-spec-3337` (#3337): within 30 seconds of the claim, `events.jsonl` held three foreign lines — a `claude-tweaks:dispatch` `skill_invoked` and two `session-end` events from sessions `2a784df0…` and `57ef0028…`, all `"attribution":"fallback"` — and `flow-preflight.js` reported `case: 3` with backfills `worktree registration, PR-early lifecycle, materialize commit`. The orchestrator had to override the case by hand.

## Deliverables

- `isUnadoptedMint` treats a directory whose `decisions.md` classifies as `claim-log-only` (`bin/lib/log-decision/claim-log.js` `classifyDecisions`) and that has no `run-state.json` as still unadopted, so fallback attribution never targets it.
- `computeAdoption` ignores `events.jsonl` lines carrying `"attribution":"fallback"` when deciding `hasOtherContent` (only `env`/`session`-attributed events are evidence this run did anything).
- A regression test for each: a claim-log-only mint is skipped by the fallback resolver; a mint whose `events.jsonl` holds only fallback-attributed lines adopts as case 2.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With a minted run dir holding only a Step 2.8 claim line, a hook event from a different session with no `PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` is not appended to that dir's `events.jsonl`.
2. `flow-preflight.js --run <dir>` on a dir with a claim-log-only `decisions.md` and an `events.jsonl` holding only `"attribution":"fallback"` lines reports `adoption.value.case === 2`.
3. A dir whose `events.jsonl` holds an `env`- or `session`-attributed line still reports `hasOtherContent: true`.

## Release Note

A freshly claimed `/flow` run no longer picks up other sessions' hook events, and no longer misreads them as an interrupted earlier run.

_Filed by `reflect` via specShapedBody._

# Reflect — staged finding 4

**Category:** tangential

Origin: reflect light from #2927

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` reads open-items ledger rows with `row.split('|')` (line 339), then takes `cells[3]` as the Status. GFM tables escape a literal pipe inside a cell as `\|`, but the split does not honor the escape. An escaped pipe in the Item cell shifts every later cell, so the Status the pack reads is a fragment of the Item text.

Observed on #2927's wrap-up, 2026-10-17: ledger row 12's Item quoted `Surface: web\|mobile\|desktop`. `wrap-up-pack.js` reported `unrecognized: 1` with value `mobile\`. The row's real status was `open`.

The dangerous case is an **open** row with an escaped pipe. It counts as `unrecognized`, not `open`, so `pack.ledger.open` under-counts. The nothing-left-behind gate's open-item enforcement then misses it, and only #2080's non-blocking warning line shows anything is wrong.

`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/ledger-write.js`'s `flipLedgerRow` (line 106) splits the same way. It refuses a row whose cell count is not 7, so it fails loudly: an escaped-pipe row cannot be resolved through it.

## Deliverables

1. One shared ledger-row cell splitter that treats `\|` as a literal pipe inside a cell. It splits only on unescaped `|` and keeps the escape intact when serializing back.
2. Use it in `pack.js`'s ledger count and in `ledger-write.js`'s `flipLedgerRow`. Check the repo's other ledger-table readers and point any that split rows the same way at it too.
3. Tests: a row whose Item cell holds `a\|b` counts under its real status in the pack, and `flipLedgerRow` resolves it without the shape refusal. The serialized row must keep the `\|`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An open ledger row whose Item contains `\|` is counted as `open` by `wrap-up-pack.js`, not `unrecognized`.
- `flipLedgerRow` resolves such a row, and the written row is byte-identical apart from the Status and Resolution cells.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Wrap-up no longer miscounts an open ledger item whose text contains an escaped pipe, so it can't slip past the nothing-left-behind check.

_Filed by `reflect`. Close to resolve; label `wontfix` to suppress future reports of this finding._

`plugin/skills/_shared/integration-model.md`'s "Run-scoped stability" says a run pins `integration-model` into its own `config.yml`. Nothing writes that pin: `bin/set-config.js` refuses the key because it is not a Manifesto lever, and the Manifesto's 13-lever batch omits it.

- `set-config.js` accepts `integration-model` (or the Manifesto writes it through the same path it uses for its levers).

Fixed: pr-first runs now record their integration model, so the PR-bookend checks actually run instead of silently skipping.

# Reflect — staged finding 1

**Category:** tangential

Origin: reflect full (batch) from #2702, #2727, #2776

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/bin/check-artifact-overwrite.js` (`bin/lib/flow/artifact-overwrite-check.js`) is the multi-spec HARD-GATE run before the consolidated Review Console. It clears a later commit's deletions on another spec's journey/story file only by two tests: same-spec self-edit (`git blame` to the same `refs #N`) or list reflow (every deleted line a `- ` entry). A content-preserving markup conversion passes neither.

In run 2026-10-16T173115-spec-2702-2727-2776, review lens 3a found this run's three journeys used numbered-list steps instead of the canonical `### N.` step headers (`_shared/diataxis-genre-templates.md`). The fix commit `80e3dad2d` (refs #2776) converted all three. The gate flagged the #2702 and #2727 journeys as overwrites, even though both files are identical once step markup is normalized. Clearing it took a manual normalization script and a human HARD-GATE ruling.

## Deliverables

- Add a third clearing test to `artifact-overwrite-check.js`: a later commit whose removed and added lines on the path are equal once journey step markup is normalized (`N. **Name** — x` / `### N. Name — x`, list indentation) is a reformat, not an overwrite.
- Fixture coverage in `tests/bin-lib/flow/artifact-overwrite-check.test.js`: a cross-spec list-to-header conversion with zero content change passes; the same conversion that also drops a step still fails.
- Update `flow/multispec-artifact-namespacing.md`'s "Append vs. overwrite" section to name the third test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Replaying the check over this run's range (`--base d81250829` through `80e3dad2d`) exits 0 with `overwrites: []`.
- A fixture where a later spec's commit converts step markup and also deletes a step body still exits 1 naming that commit.
- `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Let the multi-spec overwrite check pass a journey reformat that changes markup but no content.

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:feedback` (and the `by:feedback` records it files) keeps attributing the Claude Code harness's own worktree-session Bash refusals ("too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree", "a value computed at runtime … cannot be shown not to be git", "names git in a form too complex to verify") to `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/pre-tool-use.js`. Origin: ledger resolve gate

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

Under pr-first, `wrap-up/verification-brief.md` Step 4 posts each above-floor record's Verification Brief to the run's PR as the `brief` run comment (`<!-- run-comment: brief -->`, `_shared/pr-run-comments.md`). The marker is not spec-qualified. In a multi-spec `/claude-tweaks:flow` bundle, every spec shares one PR, so the second above-floor spec's brief finds and overwrites the first one's. `verdict` and, since #2821, `try-it` already take a `:{spec}` suffix under multi-spec.

Two readers depend on the unqualified marker. `bin/lib/wrap-up/engine-verify.js`'s acceptance-labeling check reads the `brief` comment to confirm it posted. `/claude-tweaks:demo`'s PR run-comment lookup (`demo/entry-paths.md`, added by #2821) reads it back as the record's brief, so in a bundle it can show a sibling spec's brief. Raised by #2821's whole-branch review (I3); refs #2821.

## Deliverables

1. Post the brief as `<!-- run-comment: brief:{spec} -->` when `$MULTISPEC_PARENT_DIR` is set (`verification-brief.md` Step 4), mirroring the `verdict:{spec}` rule, and add the multi-spec form to `_shared/pr-run-comments.md`'s kinds.

2. Make `engine-verify.js` and `demo/entry-paths.md`'s PR lookup read `brief:{n}` first, then fall back to plain `brief`, so single-spec runs and briefs posted before this change still resolve.

## Acceptance Criteria

- In a two-spec bundle with both specs above the floor, the PR carries two brief comments, one per spec, and neither overwrites the other.

- `/claude-tweaks:demo #N` on a bundled spec renders that spec's own brief.

- A single-spec run still posts and reads the unqualified `brief` marker.

- `npm test` passes, including a test for the `brief:{spec}` marker and the fallback read.

## Release Note

Multi-spec runs no longer overwrite one spec's Verification Brief with another's on the shared PR.

Origin: reflect full mode from #3249 (Surprises + Near-misses lenses)

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

**Related:** #3326

## Current State

During #3249's review (14 lens agents, 7 reproduction pairs at `review-effort: high`), lens 3a's (Convention) reproduction pair disagreed: one agent (3a-A) returned no findings; the other (3a-B) returned `STATUS: BLOCKED`, citing several specific functions, exports, and parameters as "completely missing from the codebase" — with exact line-number citations drawn from the record's own materialized plan file (which shows the code to add). Every one of those claims was false: direct `grep` against the live worktree confirmed every named item already existed exactly as claimed-missing (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/pr-state.js:242,326`; `release-merged.js:16,360,365,385`; `archive-merged.js:320`). The agent appears to have conflated the plan document's own illustrative "add this code" listing with the code's current applied state.

The reproduction-pair mechanism (`plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md`) correctly flagged this as a disagreement, but its own handling treats *any* disagreement as `unconfirmed`/low-confidence, which is the right default for a genuine judgment call but is not the cheapest-available resolution for this specific claim shape: "a named function/export/parameter does not exist" is mechanically, cheaply verifiable (one `grep`/`Read`) before ever reaching a human at the Review Console. Without an explicit instruction to do that check, a differently-briefed session could plausibly have accepted the disagreement as "needs a human to judge" and left a factually-false BLOCKED claim staged as merely low-confidence, sending a human to investigate a non-existent gap.

## Deliverables

- Add one sentence to `step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s dispatch prompt template (or the CALIBRATION block) instructing lens agents not to infer code absence from a plan/spec document's own illustrative code listings — verify a "missing code" claim by reading the actual target file directly.
- Add a narrow, mechanical escape hatch to the reproduction-pair disagreement-handling procedure: when one side of a disagreement asserts code/export/parameter *absence* at a named `path:line`/symbol, the dispatching session runs one `grep`/`Read` check against the live target file before staging the finding as `unconfirmed` — a contradicted "missing" claim resolves straight to "refuted, not staged" rather than "low-confidence, staged."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A reproduction-pair disagreement where one side asserts code/export/parameter absence that a one-command `grep`/`Read` check can mechanically refute no longer reaches the Wrap-Up Review Console as a merely low-confidence item — it resolves to refuted before routing.
- [ ] The dispatch prompt template explicitly warns against inferring code state from a plan/spec document's own code listings.

## Release Note

Review's reproduction-pair handling gains a cheap ground-truth check for mechanically-falsifiable "code is missing" disagreements, reducing false BLOCKED verdicts reaching the Review Console.

Origin: reflect full (batch) from #3072,#3003

Defer-reason: tangential

**Related:** #3329

## Current State

`bin/lib/coordination.js` `categoriseReproduction` pairs a same-location candidate (path exact, line ±2) only when `sameSubstance` is not `false`. For two independently worded reports of the same issue, the substance score falls below the threshold, so a genuinely reproduced finding comes out as two `nearLocation` unconfirmed entries.

Observed three times: #3023 (lens 3b, `release.js` `merge-base --is-ancestor` missing `--end-of-options`), #3028 (lens 3f, `tests/bin-lib/compose-subject.test.js:454`, rows copied verbatim), and #3003 (lens 3c, `plugin/bin/qa-stamp.js:121` and `:132`, rows copied verbatim, both pairs split). Each time the controller fell back to the direct-verification override. Re-checked after #2955 widened the location band to ±5: the merged categoriser still returns all four #3003 entries unconfirmed, so the gap is the same-line substance test, not the band. In an unattended run where no source read happens, a reproduced medium finding routes to the Review Console's low-confidence section instead of being auto-applied under the ceiling.

## Deliverables

Make the same-substance decision robust to independent wording for same-file, same-line (±2) pairs. Options: weight shared code identifiers and backticked tokens, or treat an exact-line match plus a shared identifier as same substance.

Keep #1980's guard: two different issues at the same location must still stay split.

## Acceptance Criteria

A fixture test built from the three observed pairs (each agent's Finding text verbatim) categorises every pair as `confirmed`.

#1980's existing near-location, different-substance fixtures still come out `unconfirmed`.

## Release Note

Review reproduction pairs that report the same issue in different words are now recognized as reproduced.
