Surface: infra

**Related:** #3429, #3440, #3505, #3506, #3507, #3509, #3517, #3518, #2713, #2767, #3187, #3396, #3500

## Current State

The post-merge `windows-regression` workflow (run 39105151251, on `windows-latest`) found one test file newly failing after PR #3428 merged as `21ef3dc91`. That commit (#3400's change) added `tests/wrap-up-multispec-defer-still-live.test.js`; the file does not exist at the base `ac7ba9360`, so this failure is genuinely new rather than an inherited one. Exactly one test in it fails: `the defer paragraph is still found as one paragraph under CRLF line endings` (line 61), with `expected exactly one MULTISPEC_REVIEW_DEFER branch paragraph` / `0 !== 1`. Verified against `origin/main` at `7852fd8bf`, where the test file is unchanged since `21ef3dc91`.

Root cause, test-side only. The test's `live()` helper (line 23) reads `plugin/skills/wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md` with a raw `fs.readFileSync(FILE, 'utf8')`. The CRLF test (line 62) then builds its CRLF input with `live().replace(/\n/g, '\r\n')`. On a Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` the read already returns `\r\n` line endings (this repo's `.gitattributes` pins only `tools/upstream-drift/fixtures/**`), so the replace turns every `\r\n` into `\r\r\n`. `deferParagraph`'s split regex `/\r?\n\r?\n/` cannot match a `\r\r\n\r\r\n` paragraph break, the file never splits into paragraphs, and no chunk starts with `**MULTISPEC_REVIEW_DEFER branch:**`. Reproduced in scratch against the `origin/main` copy of the skill file: the current transform finds 1 paragraph from an LF read and 0 from a CRLF read; LF-normalizing the read first finds 1 from both.

The other tests in the file pass on a CRLF checkout and are out of scope: `deferParagraph(live())` already splits on `\r?\n`, `SENTENCE` is a single line, and the engine-source pins (`checkBody`'s `'\n});'` search and the one-line skip pin) hold under `\r\n`. A repo-wide grep of `tests/` for `.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n')` on `origin/main` found no other site applying it to a live file read: every other hit converts an in-test string literal (`tests/bin-lib/flow/pr-body-premise-reversal.test.js`, `tests/comment-trust-conformance.test.js`, `tests/bin-lib/verify/extract.test.js` and others), which is the pattern the `windows-checkout-test-parity` project skill prescribes.

## Deliverables

1. `tests/wrap-up-multispec-defer-still-live.test.js`: LF-normalize the live read before any CRLF conversion, so the CRLF test builds its input from LF text on every checkout. Preferred move: route `live()` through `tests/helpers/read-skill.js`'s `readText()`, the shared EOL-normalizing read that prose-conformance suites already use (#2763), so every test in the file reads LF text and the CRLF test's `.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n')` produces exactly one `\r\n` per line break. An inline `.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n')` at the CRLF test's call site is the acceptable fallback if routing `live()` would change another test's behavior; state which was chosen in the PR body.
2. Keep the CRLF test meaningful: it must still feed `deferParagraph` a genuinely CRLF string (assert or otherwise make sure the input contains `\r\n` and no `\r\r\n`), so it keeps pinning that the extractor's split survives CRLF.
3. Before opening the PR, re-run the grep for `.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n')` (and `split('\n\n')` / `indexOf('\n\n'` on a raw live read) across `tests/` and fix any new hit that converts a raw live file read, with the same move. It was clean at shaping time against `origin/main` `7852fd8bf`; record the result in the PR body.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `node --test tests/wrap-up-multispec-defer-still-live.test.js` passes on macOS/Linux with no test skipped or removed.
- [ ] The same file passes on `windows-latest`. Prove it before merge by dispatching `gh workflow run windows-regression.yml --ref {branch}` and quoting the run's result for this file. A non-main ref never files an issue. If the dispatch cannot run, say so explicitly. Do not treat an in-process CRLF simulation as a Windows run.
- [ ] On Linux, a CRLF-checkout simulation of the fixed test passes: run the CRLF test's logic against the skill file's text converted to `\r\n` first (for example, a scratch copy written with CRLF endings and read through the same helper), and it finds exactly one paragraph. Against the pre-fix transform, the same simulation finds zero.
- [ ] The CRLF test still discriminates: temporarily rename the `**MULTISPEC_REVIEW_DEFER branch:**` lead-in in `plugin/skills/wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md` and the test goes red; restore the file in the same command.
- [ ] No file under `plugin/` changes. The skill prose is correct; only the test's input construction is wrong.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fixed a wrap-up conformance test that failed on Windows checkouts because it converted already-CRLF text to CRLF a second time.

## Technical Approach

Test-side only, following `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md`'s "Build CRLF inputs from the LF text" rule: a CRLF case must be built from the LF string with `.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n')`. A raw read of a tracked file is not LF text on a Windows checkout, so the read has to be normalized first. `tests/helpers/read-skill.js`'s `readText()` (`fs.readFileSync(absPath, 'utf8').replace(/\r\n/g, '\n')`) is the repo's single normalizing read for exactly this case. The skill's Anti-Patterns row for doctoring a go-red control on a raw read (`tests/wrap-up-record-resolution-conformance.test.js`, #3395) is the same move applied to the same class of defect. The engine-source reads (`engineSource()`) need no change.

### Key Files

- `tests/wrap-up-multispec-defer-still-live.test.js` — `live()` (line 23) routed through `readText()`, or the CRLF test (line 62) LF-normalizes before converting
- `tests/helpers/read-skill.js` — read-only reference: the shared `readText()` EOL-normalizing read
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/execution-and-verification.md` — read-only reference: the `**MULTISPEC_REVIEW_DEFER branch:**` paragraph (line 9) the test extracts

## Gotchas

- Do not "fix" this by loosening `deferParagraph`'s split regex to tolerate `\r\r\n`. That would hide a malformed fixture rather than build a correct one, and `\r\r\n` never occurs in a real checkout.
- Do not add a `.gitattributes` `eol=lf` rule for the skill file or `tests/` as the fix. The parity skill keeps `.gitattributes` scoped to the hashed upstream fixtures on purpose, and the CRLF test exists precisely to prove the extractor survives a CRLF checkout.
- This is one of several open `Windows regression:` records (#3429, #3440, #3505, #3506, #3507, #3509, #3517, #3518), each for a different commit and different files. Keep this record to `tests/wrap-up-multispec-defer-still-live.test.js` and its sibling grep.

## Original request

Windows regression: 1 test file(s) newly failing after 21ef3dc91

The post-merge Windows check failed on commit 21ef3dc9182b700efd234db073a26ebc3bfdbd9c (compared against ac7ba9360).

**Merged PR:** #3428 (https://github.com/thn-inc/claude-tweaks/pull/3428)

**Run:** https://github.com/thn-inc/claude-tweaks/actions/runs/39105151251

### Newly failing test files
- `tests/wrap-up-multispec-defer-still-live.test.js`

### Failure excerpts

#### `tests/wrap-up-multispec-defer-still-live.test.js`

```
not ok 12400 - the defer paragraph is still found as one paragraph under CRLF line endings
  ---
  duration_ms: 1.7158
  type: 'test'
  location: 'D:\\a\\claude-tweaks\\claude-tweaks\\tests\\wrap-up-multispec-defer-still-live.test.js:61:1'
  failureType: 'testCodeFailure'
  error: |-
    expected exactly one MULTISPEC_REVIEW_DEFER branch paragraph
    
    0 !== 1
    
  code: 'ERR_ASSERTION'
```

_Filed by .github/workflows/windows-regression.yml — failures were compared against the push's base commit (verify.js --baseline). Shape it with /claude-tweaks:specify before building._

groups.title: Windows regression: 1 test file(s) newly failing after 21ef3dc91

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #2767, #3315, #3429, #3458, #3461, #3505, #3506, #3507, #3509, #3517, #3518, #3523

## Current State

The post-merge `windows-regression` workflow flagged `tests/bin-lib/timing/cli.test.js` as newly failing after ffe20b982 (#3406, per-dispatch cost attribution for #3375), run https://github.com/thn-inc/claude-tweaks/actions/runs/39061373299. The run's own `verify-report` artifact shows the real picture. The issue body's excerpt does not.

- **Base commit 6a25dc724 (baseline log):** 2 failing tests, `#1929 AC4: --auto-transcript locates…` (line 113) and `#1929 whole-branch review fix 2: … (mode 000)` (line 170). Both failures predate this merge.
- **Head commit ffe20b982 (isolated log, and the isolated retry, which matches it exactly):** 7 failing tests, the same 2 plus 5 new ones from #3375: `#3375 AC3.1` (line 210), `#3375 AC3.2` (line 234), `#3375 AC4: a not-found dispatch…` (line 242), `#3375 AC4: an empty transcript…` (line 255), and `#3375: with several transcripts…` (line 313).

The issue's excerpt quotes the pre-existing `#1929 AC4` failure because `tools/windows-regression/file-issue.js`'s `excerptFor` takes the first `not ok` naming the file, not the first newly failing one.

All three causes are in the test file. The production code in `plugin/bin/phase-timing.js` and `plugin/bin/lib/timing/transcript.js` behaves correctly on Windows:

1. **The fixture home is set through `HOME` alone.** The `#1929 AC4` test (lines 121 and 126) and the `subagentRun()` helper (line 203) point the CLI at a temporary home with `env: { ...process.env, HOME: home }`. `locateTranscripts` defaults `homeDir` to `os.homedir()` (`transcript.js:41`). On Windows, `os.homedir()` reads `USERPROFILE`, not `HOME`, so the CLI searches the runner's real profile. The CI output says `tokens: transcript not found (no sess-1.jsonl under the worktree slug directory)`. This breaks `#1929 AC4` (pre-existing), `#3375 AC3.1`, and both `#3375 AC4` tests. `tests/statusline.test.js:932` already records the same Windows behavior.
2. **The golden files are read raw from a CRLF checkout.** `#3375 AC3.1` (line 214) and `#3375 AC3.2` (line 238) read `tests/fixtures/timing/subagents-golden-auto.md` and `subagents-golden-plain.md` with a bare `fs.readFileSync`. Under `core.autocrlf=true` those files carry `\r\n`, while the CLI writes `\n`. The AC3.2 diff in the CI log differs only in line endings. `.gitattributes` exempts only `tools/upstream-drift/fixtures/**`.
3. **A path is matched with a forward-slash regex.** The `#3375: with several transcripts…` test (lines 322 and 324) matches `/…sess-2\/subagents$/`. `readDispatches` names the native `fs` path, which on Windows is `…\sess-2\subagents`. CI actual: `no subagents/ directory at D:\a\_temp\ct-timing-home-EQjibG\.claude\projects\-Users-x-Code-repo--claude-worktrees-wt\sess-2\subagents`.

The pre-existing `fix 2` failure (line 170) has a different cause. It makes a file unreadable with `fs.chmodSync(…, 0o000)`, which on Windows only toggles the read-only attribute, so the read succeeds. It is skipped only under root (`skipUnderRoot`), never on win32.

## Deliverables

1. Point every fixture-home child process in `tests/bin-lib/timing/cli.test.js` at the temporary home on both platforms. Set `USERPROFILE: home` beside `HOME: home` in the `#1929 AC4` test's two `spawnSync` env objects (lines 121 and 126) and in `subagentRun()`'s returned `env` (line 203). In the same objects, drop any inherited `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, for example `const { CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, ...base } = process.env`. That keeps the tests hermetic once #3458 makes `locateTranscripts` honor that variable.
2. Read both golden files through `tests/helpers/read-skill.js`'s `readText` (it normalizes `\r\n` to `\n`) instead of a raw `fs.readFileSync`, in `#3375 AC3.1` (line 214) and `#3375 AC3.2` (line 238).
3. Build the expected path in `#3375: with several transcripts…` from the native separator: `path.join(s.slugDir, 'sess-2', 'subagents')`, compared exactly against `d.notFoundDirs[0]` and against the stdout line. Do not use `/`.
4. Give `#1929 whole-branch review fix 2` (line 170) an explicit win32 skip with a stated reason alongside its existing root skip, so a Windows run reports it as skipped rather than failed. Do not end the test early with a silent `return`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/bin-lib/timing/cli.test.js` contains no child-process env that sets `HOME` without also setting `USERPROFILE` to the same value (grep `HOME: home` and confirm each hit sits beside `USERPROFILE: home`). None of those env objects carries `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.
- [ ] Neither golden fixture is read with a bare `fs.readFileSync`; both go through `readText`.
- [ ] The two `sess-2\/subagents` regexes are gone, and both assertions compare against a `path.join`-built path.
- [ ] Reversion proof for the CRLF fix, recorded in the PR: a CRLF copy of `subagents-golden-plain.md` (built from the LF text with `.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n')`) read through `readText` still satisfies `#3375 AC3.2`’s equality, and the same copy read raw fails it. The `USERPROFILE` and native-path fixes cannot be made to fail on a POSIX host, where `os.homedir()` follows `HOME` and `path.join` uses `/`, so the Windows run below is their only proof. Say this in the PR rather than claiming a local reversion.
- [ ] `node --test tests/bin-lib/timing/cli.test.js` passes on macOS/Linux with zero failures (raw summary lines quoted in the PR).
- [ ] On the next `windows-regression` run after merge, `tests/bin-lib/timing/cli.test.js` is not in `baselineAdjudicated.attributable`. The isolated log shows 0 failures for the file, with `fix 2` reported as skipped on win32.

## Release Note

Fix the phase-timing CLI tests so they pass on a Windows checkout.

## Technical Approach

Test-only change in one file. Each fix follows a pattern this repo already uses (`.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md`):

- **Home override:** `os.homedir()` resolves `USERPROFILE` on win32 and `HOME` elsewhere, so setting both keys to the fixture home makes the override effective on every platform. No production change and no new `--home` flag is needed: `locateTranscripts` already takes an injectable `homeDir`, and the CLI's use of `os.homedir()` is correct behavior.
- **CRLF goldens:** reuse `readText` from `tests/helpers/read-skill.js` (#2763's shared EOL-normalizing read). The CLI's own output is `\n`, which is the contract. The golden file's working-copy line endings are a checkout artifact, so normalize at the read.
- **Native path expectation:** the `notFound` text names an `fs` path, which is native by contract, not a display ID. So fix the expectation with `path.join`, per the skill's "Display IDs and native paths are two contracts" rule, and leave the producer alone.
- **Mode-000 test:** combine the existing `skipUnderRoot(...)` result with a `process.platform === 'win32'` reason (for example, `{ skip: (IS_ROOT && 'root ignores file permissions') || (process.platform === 'win32' && 'win32: chmod 0o000 only sets the read-only attribute') }`), matching the explicit-skip convention in `tests/helpers/root.js`.

### Key Files

- `tests/bin-lib/timing/cli.test.js`: add `USERPROFILE` to the three fixture-home env objects, read the goldens via `readText`, use a `path.join` expectation in the several-transcripts test, and add a win32 skip on the mode-000 test.
- `tests/helpers/read-skill.js`: reused as-is (`readText`), no change.
- `tests/fixtures/timing/subagents-golden-auto.md`: unchanged; now read via `readText`.
- `tests/fixtures/timing/subagents-golden-plain.md`: unchanged; now read via `readText`.

## Gotchas

- Do not "fix" this in `plugin/bin/lib/timing/transcript.js` or `plugin/bin/phase-timing.js`. Both behave correctly on Windows. A production `HOME` preference would diverge from where Claude Code itself writes transcripts on win32.
- The issue body's excerpt shows a failure that also existed at the base commit. Judge the fix by the 7-vs-2 failing-test diff in the run's `verify-report` artifact, not by the excerpt (`docs/donts.md` `[IL-160]`).
- The other root-cause fix in this file, adding a `.gitattributes` `eol=lf` rule for `tests/fixtures/timing/*.md`, was considered and rejected. It changes the checkout of every Windows clone for one suite, while `readText` is the repo's established per-read normalization.
- Interaction with #3458, which is `ready` and makes `locateTranscripts` honor `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. These fixture-home spawns copy `process.env`, so once #3458 lands, a `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set on the developer machine or runner would override the fixture home on every platform. Whichever of the two lands second must also remove `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` from these env objects. Deliverable 1 does this already. If #3458 lands first and adds its own handling, keep a single removal, not two.
- `tools/windows-regression/file-issue.js`'s `excerptFor` picks the first `not ok` for an attributable file even when that test also failed at the base. This misleading excerpt is a separate defect in the filer and out of scope here.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #3429, #3440, #3506, #3507, #3509, #3517, #3518, #3523, #2713, #2767, #3187, #3315, #3396, #3442

## Current State

The post-merge `windows-regression` workflow (run 39101872855, on `windows-latest`) found three test files newly failing after PR #3434 merged as `2a0b7f65a`. PR #3434 shipped #3370's unattended-console residue feature. The production code is correct on Windows. Every failure is a test assertion that hard-codes `/` as the path separator, for a path that the code under test builds natively with `path.join` / `path.resolve`. On Windows that path comes out as `D:\a\...\pipelines\...`. Verified against `origin/main` at `7852fd8bf`, where none of the three files has changed since `2a0b7f65a`:

- `tests/bin-lib/console/cli.test.js:382`: the `#3370` "Needs a human" test pins the trailing `paths move when the run is archived` line with ``new RegExp(`... node "/.+/bin/console-residue\\.js" --run "/.+/${path.basename(fx.runDir)}"$`)``. The producer is `plugin/bin/console-resolve.js:39`'s `needsAHumanBlock`, which prints `${pluginRoot}/bin/console-residue.js` (pluginRoot comes from `path.resolve`, so on Windows it is backslash-separated with a literal `/bin/...` tail) and `--run "${runDir}"` (native). The leading `"/` and the `/` separators in the regex never match a `D:\...` path.
- `tests/bin-lib/console/residue-cli.test.js:160`: the `MOVED` regex expects `.*/pipelines/{run} has moved to .*/pipelines/archive/{run}`. `plugin/bin/console-residue.js`'s pre-archive fallback prints `o.run` (the test builds it with `path.join`) and `archiveDir` (`path.join`), both native. `MOVED` is asserted at lines 169 and 179. Line 169 failed. Line 179's test (`--ack given the pre-archive path ...`) asserts the same regex and must be fixed too.
- `tests/bin-lib/console/residue.test.js:108`: `lines.includes(`    cat "${dir}/staged/review-13-record.md"`)`. `plugin/bin/lib/console/residue.js`'s `itemLines` builds that path with `path.join(consoleDir, 'staged', item.id)`. The same `${dir}/...` shape appears at lines 121, 129, 172 and 182 (the `spec-12/staged`, `… and 2 more — see`, `(no id)` and `see "${dir}/decisions.md"` tests). The run reported only the first failure in the file, so those lines are latent failures of the same class.

These are native filesystem paths printed as paste-ready commands, not display IDs. `windows-checkout-test-parity`'s "Display IDs and native paths are two contracts" rule therefore puts the fix on the test side: build the expected value with `path.join` / `path.resolve`, the same way the code under test does. The producers are not normalized to `/`.

## Deliverables

1. `tests/bin-lib/console/cli.test.js`: rewrite the line-382 assertion so it holds on any separator. It must still pin the whole line, anchored at both ends: the `paths move when the run is archived; current paths:` prefix, the `console-residue.js` command and the `--run` value ending in the fixture run's basename. Either build the exact expected string from the plugin root (`path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', 'plugin')`) and `fx.runDir` (already `realpathSync`ed by `mainCheckoutWithRun`), or keep a regex with `[\\/]` separator classes in place of every literal `/` and an escaped basename.
2. `tests/bin-lib/console/residue-cli.test.js`: rewrite `MOVED` (line 160) so both tests that assert it (lines 169 and 179) match a native-separator stderr line. Keep the `pipelines` → `pipelines/archive` distinction and the `\n$` end anchor.
3. `tests/bin-lib/console/residue.test.js`: build every expected path at lines 108, 121, 129, 172 and 182 with `path.join(dir, ...)`, keeping exact `lines.includes` / `deepStrictEqual` matching. The `"/p/bin/console-residue.js"` pins at lines 111 and 150 stay literal: `formatResidueLines` concatenates `pluginRoot` with `/bin/...` and never joins it, so they already pass on Windows.
4. Before opening the PR, re-run the separator-shape grep (template paths like `${dir}/...`, and the regex fragments `"/.+/` and `.*/`) over the other suites that cover this feature: `tests/bin-lib/hooks/session-residue.test.js`, `tests/console-resolve-conformance.test.js`, `tests/hooks-session-start.test.js` and `tests/hooks-dispatcher.test.js`. It was clean at shaping time against `origin/main` `7852fd8bf`. Fix any new hit with the same move, and record the result in the PR body.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `node --test tests/bin-lib/console/cli.test.js tests/bin-lib/console/residue-cli.test.js tests/bin-lib/console/residue.test.js` passes on macOS/Linux with no test skipped or removed.
- [ ] The same three files pass on `windows-latest`. Prove it before merge by dispatching `gh workflow run windows-regression.yml --ref {branch}` and quoting the run's result for those three files. A non-main ref never files an issue (the filer's own header comment). If the dispatch cannot run, say so explicitly. Do not treat a `path.win32` simulation as a Windows run.
- [ ] Each rewritten assertion still discriminates. Temporarily change the producer's output: drop `archive` from `archiveDir` in `console-residue.js`, change `staged` to `stage` in `residue.js`'s `itemLines`, and drop the `--run` value from `console-resolve.js:39`. The matching test must go red on Linux in each case. Restore the producer in the same command.
- [ ] No production file under `plugin/` changes. The producers already emit native paths, which is the correct contract.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fixed three console-residue tests that failed on Windows because they expected forward-slash paths.

## Technical Approach

Test-side only, following `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md`. "Display IDs and native paths are two contracts" says to build the expected value with `path.join`/`path.resolve` when the code under test joins the path. Its Anti-Patterns row says not to expect a POSIX absolute literal where the code resolves the path. Prefer exact strings built from fixture paths over loosened regexes wherever the fixture knows the real path, as `residue.test.js` and `residue-cli.test.js`'s `--ack --run "${fs.realpathSync(f.runDir)}"` pin already do. Where a regex stays necessary (a temp root or a `mainCheckoutRoot`-derived prefix the test cannot predict), replace each literal `/` separator with `[\\/]` and pass interpolated path fragments through a regex escape.

### Key Files

- `tests/bin-lib/console/cli.test.js` — line 382's `paths move when the run is archived` regex made separator-agnostic
- `tests/bin-lib/console/residue-cli.test.js` — `MOVED` regex (line 160) made separator-agnostic for both tests that assert it
- `tests/bin-lib/console/residue.test.js` — expected `cat`/`see` paths at lines 108, 121, 129, 172 and 182 built with `path.join`
- `plugin/bin/console-resolve.js` — read-only reference: `needsAHumanBlock` (line 39) is the producer of the cli.test.js line
- `plugin/bin/console-residue.js` — read-only reference: the pre-archive `has moved to` stderr producer
- `plugin/bin/lib/console/residue.js` — read-only reference: `itemLines`/`formatResidueLines` path producers

## Gotchas

- Do not "fix" this by normalizing the producers to `/`. These are paths a human pastes into a shell, and native separators are correct there. `toPosix` is for display IDs only (the parity skill's Decision Framework row). The mixed `D:\...\plugin/bin/console-residue.js` that `${pluginRoot}/bin/...` produces on Windows is valid for `node` and is out of scope here.
- On macOS, `os.tmpdir()` sits behind a `/var` → `/private/var` symlink. `cli.test.js`'s fixture already `realpathSync`s its root, but `residue-cli.test.js`'s second `MOVED` test derives `mainRoot` from cwd via `mainCheckoutRoot`, so an exact-string pin there must use the same resolved form or stay a separator-agnostic regex.
- On `windows-latest`, the checkout is on `D:` and `os.tmpdir()` is on `C:` (the parity skill's real-runner section). Any expected prefix must come from the fixture's own paths, never from a hard-coded drive or root.
- This is one of several open `Windows regression:` records (#3506, #3507, #3509, #3517, #3518, #3523, #3440, #3429), each for a different commit and different files. Keep this record to the three console-residue suites and their sibling greps.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

## Current State

`.github/workflows/windows-regression.yml` flagged `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/pr-state.test.js` and `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/release-merged.test.js` after 5cf9073d3 (PR #3439, which shipped #3412). The production code is not at fault. Every failure in both files comes from how the tests fake `gh`, and the fake does not work on a Windows checkout.

The issue's two excerpts are misleading. The run's `verify-report` artifact (run 39101659988) shows that both quoted tests also fail at the base commit f49277005. They are `pr-state.test.js:35` ("merged PR wins over other PRs for the same branch") and `release-merged.test.js:242` ("Phase 1.5 resolves prState via the pool…"). The excerpt quotes only the first failure in each file, and the filer flagged the files because #3412 added new tests that fail for the same reason. Per-file counts, run in isolation:

| File | Base f49277005 | HEAD 5cf9073d3 | Newly failing (all added by #3412) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pr-state.test.js` | 20 of 38 fail | 22 of 40 fail | lines 529 and 542 (`request closingIssuesReferences…`) |
| `release-merged.test.js` | 7 of 25 fail | 17 of 50 fail | line 381 (by-number fallback keeps the claim…), lines 938, 952, 965, 978, 993, 1004, 1017 (the `run3348Scenario` tests), and lines 1113, 1129 (the `runTwoCandidateScenario` tests) |

(Line numbers are from `origin/main` 7852fd8bf. Neither file has changed since 5cf9073d3.)

There are two causes, both Windows-only:

1. **A `#!/bin/sh` file named `gh` on PATH is never spawned.** `pr-state.js` calls `execFileSync('gh', …)` and `execFile('gh', …)` with no injection point. The tests put a script named `gh` (no extension) first on PATH: `installGhWrapper` at `pr-state.test.js:17`, plus `installArgvSpy` and `installArgvLoggingGhWrapper`, and inline `wrapperPath = path.join(wrapperDir, 'gh')` blocks in `release-merged.test.js`, including the shared `run3348Scenario` (line 869) and `runTwoCandidateScenario` (line 1035). On win32, Node looks up an extensionless command by appending `.com` and `.exe`, so the stub is skipped. Even if it were found, Windows cannot run a shell script directly. The tests then get a transport classification (`'gh-absent'`/`'network-failure'`) instead of the stub's JSON. That matches every error in the logs: `undefined !== 2`, `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')`, and `{"reason":"network-failure"}` skips in `release-merged`.
2. **POSIX literal `'/tmp'` used as `repoRoot`/cwd.** `pr-state.test.js` passes `'/tmp'` 61 times. On a Windows checkout `/tmp` resolves to `{drive}:\tmp`, which does not exist. The by-number resolvers' #3029 guard (`classifyByNumberError` in `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/pr-state.js`, around line 137) then reports `'invalid-arguments'`. So the three stub-free "gh absent -> gh-absent" tests (lines 300, 381, 489) fail with `+ 'invalid-arguments' - 'gh-absent'`.

Precedent: `tests/console-execute.test.js` (#3358) uses the same PATH-stub technique, cites `pr-state.test.js` as its source, and already skips those tests on win32 (`{ skip: process.platform === 'win32' }`, line 443 onward).

**Related:** #2767, #3412, #3416, #3429, #3440, #3491, #3505, #3507, #3509, #3517, #3518, #3523

## Deliverables

1. In `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/pr-state.test.js`, replace the POSIX literal `'/tmp'` passed as `repoRoot` with a real directory (`os.tmpdir()`, held in one module-level constant). Leave the deliberately nonexistent paths alone: `'/definitely/not/here'` and `'/tmp/definitely-not-a-repo-xyz'`.
2. In both files, skip every test that depends on a `gh` stub on PATH when running on win32, with a stated reason. Use one per-file constant, for example `const PATH_STUB_SKIP = process.platform === 'win32' && 'win32: execFileSync("gh") never spawns a #!/bin/sh stub named gh on PATH'`. This covers the tests that call `installGhWrapper` / `installArgvSpy` / `installArgvLoggingGhWrapper`, the inline wrapper blocks, and every test that runs through `run3348Scenario` or `runTwoCandidateScenario`. That includes the three `pr-state` guard tests that install a spy only to assert `gh` was never called (current lines 410, 421, 455). They pass on win32 today, but vacuously, because there the spy can never observe a call. Tests that install no stub keep running on win32: the pure `decideRelease` / `prClosesIssue` / `shouldSkipClaimRead` tests, the injected-runner `resolvePrStatesBulk` tests, the falsy-number short-circuit test, and the PATH-emptied gh-absent tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `pr-state.test.js` contains no `'/tmp'` argument except inside `'/tmp/definitely-not-a-repo-xyz'`, and `grep -c "os.tmpdir()" tests/bin-lib/reconcile/pr-state.test.js` is at least its previous count plus one (the new constant).
2. Every `test(` in either file whose body, or a helper it calls, writes a `gh` file into a PATH-prepended directory carries the per-file skip constant in its options. Every test that writes no stub does not carry it.
3. On POSIX, `node --test tests/bin-lib/reconcile/pr-state.test.js tests/bin-lib/reconcile/release-merged.test.js` passes with zero skipped tests. Quote the raw `ℹ tests` / `ℹ pass` / `ℹ skipped` lines.
4. On the next `windows-latest` run of `.github/workflows/windows-regression.yml` after merge, neither file appears in `baselineAdjudicated.failingFiles` of the run's `verify-report.json` artifact. Each file's log in `verify-logs/` shows `# fail 0`, the stub-dependent tests are reported as skipped with the stated reason, and the three gh-absent by-number tests (current lines 300, 381, 489) pass rather than skip.
5. `npm test` passes on the ubuntu CI gate.

## Release Note

Fixed two reconciler test suites that failed only on Windows checkouts, with no change to plugin behavior.

## Technical Approach

- **Skip, not a production seam.** Rejected alternative: add an injectable runner to `pr-state.js`'s `resolvePrState*` functions (the `gh-api-module-pattern` seam), so the tests can stop faking `gh` through PATH. That would change a production module that `release-merged.js`, `archive-merged.js`, `reap-merged.js` and others depend on, purely for a test platform. The resolver logic is platform-neutral, and the POSIX run covers it. This matches #3429's ruling and the `windows-checkout-test-parity` skill: behavior only one platform can produce gets a `skip` with a stated reason. `tests/console-execute.test.js` already applies exactly this skip to the same stub technique.
- **`'/tmp'` -> `os.tmpdir()`.** This is the parity skill's "POSIX absolute literal" anti-pattern. A real directory lets the gh-absent tests reach their real ENOENT-for-gh branch on win32 instead of the #3029 nonexistent-directory branch. It also keeps the by-number stub tests honest on POSIX.
- Apply the skip per test (`test(name, { skip: PATH_STUB_SKIP }, fn)`), not by skipping the whole file. Each file has stub-free tests that should keep running on Windows.

### Key Files

- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/pr-state.test.js`: add `os.tmpdir()` repoRoot constant replacing `'/tmp'`, and `PATH_STUB_SKIP` on the 22 stub-installing tests
- `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/release-merged.test.js`: add `PATH_STUB_SKIP` on the 17 stub-installing tests (lines 242–713 inline wrappers, 381, the `run3348Scenario` and `runTwoCandidateScenario` callers)
- `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/pr-state.js`: read-only reference (`execFileSync('gh')` call sites, `byNumberArgsValid`, `classifyByNumberError`). No change
- `tests/console-execute.test.js`: read-only reference (existing win32 skip on the same stub technique)

## Gotchas

- The base `windows-latest` run of these two files also fails at f49277005. The run quotes pre-existing failures as its excerpts, so "did my change fix the new tests" cannot be read from the excerpt alone. Diff the per-test `not ok` set in the run's `verify-logs/` instead.
- The counts come from a scripted pass over each `test(` body checked against the HEAD logs. In `pr-state`, 22 tests install a stub: 19 fail on win32 and 3 pass vacuously. The other 3 failures there are the stub-free `'/tmp'` tests. In `release-merged`, 17 tests install a stub and all 17 fail. Surface: infra

## Current State

The post-merge Windows check (`.github/workflows/windows-regression.yml`, run 39101724698) reports one test file newly failing after commit a62e27344 (PR #3452, which added the file): `tests/manifesto-overrides-ceiling-conformance.test.js`. It passes on ubuntu CI and on any LF checkout (verified: `node --test tests/manifesto-overrides-ceiling-conformance.test.js` → 11 pass, 0 fail on macOS).

Root cause, verified against the file at `origin/main`:

- The test reads its three governed markdown inputs with raw `fs.readFileSync(..., 'utf8')` — `plugin/skills/flow/manifesto-overrides.md` and `plugin/skills/review/step3-routing.md` at lines 13-14, `plugin/skills/flow/manifesto.md` at line 95.
- `routingColumns` (line 16) does `md.split('\n')` and then ``lines.indexOf('| Severity | `none` | `low` | `medium` |')`` — an exact whole-line match. On a Windows checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` (no `.gitattributes` rule covers these files), every line keeps a trailing `\r`, so the lookup returns -1 and line 19 throws `ceiling-keyed routing table header not found in step3-routing.md`.
- The throw happens at module top level (line 67, `const cols = routingColumns(routing);`), so the whole file fails before any `test()` registers — one file-level failure, not a per-assertion one.
- Simulated: the header is found at index 44 on the LF text, -1 on the same text with `\n` replaced by `\r\n`, and 44 again after `\r\n` → `\n` normalization.

The repo already has the fix for this class: `tests/helpers/read-skill.js` exports `readText(absPath)`, an EOL-normalizing read (#2763) that about 80 test files already use for prose-conformance reads. This file, added by PR #3452, does not use it.

**Related:** #2713, #3187, #3396, #3429, #3440, #3505, #3506, #3509, #3512, #3517, #3518, #3523

## Deliverables

1. `tests/manifesto-overrides-ceiling-conformance.test.js` reads all three markdown inputs through `readText()` from `tests/helpers/read-skill.js` instead of raw `fs.readFileSync`.
2. The file's line-splitting extractors (`routingColumns`, `ceilingRow`, and the lever-7 filter in the manifesto test) split on `/\r?\n/`, so the extractor itself tolerates CRLF input, not only the read.
3. A new CRLF test case, built from the LF text with `.replace(/\n/g, '\r\n')`, asserting `routingColumns` on the CRLF text deep-equals `routingColumns` on the LF text, and that `ceilingRow` returns the same cell for each ceiling value (`none`, `low`, `medium`) on both.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `grep -n "fs.readFileSync" tests/manifesto-overrides-ceiling-conformance.test.js` returns no matches, and the file requires `readText` from `./helpers/read-skill`.
2. `node --test tests/manifesto-overrides-ceiling-conformance.test.js` passes with 0 failures: the 11 existing tests plus the new CRLF case.
3. Go-red check: temporarily changing `routingColumns`'s split back to `split('\n')` makes the new CRLF case fail, and restoring it makes it pass again.
4. CRLF checkout check: on a scratch clone made with `git clone --config core.autocrlf=true` where `git ls-files --eol plugin/skills/review/step3-routing.md` reports `w/crlf`, the file passes with `node --test`. If `w/crlf` cannot be produced on a POSIX host, record that and rely on AC 3.
5. `npm test` passes with no new failures compared to `origin/main`.

## Release Note

Fixed a test that failed on Windows checkouts because of line-ending differences.

## Technical Approach

This is a test-only change to one file, using the repo's established CRLF pattern (`windows-checkout-test-parity` project skill: "Build CRLF inputs from the LF text" and the `readText()` decision row). Replace the three raw reads with `readText(path.join(...))`. Change the three `split('\n')` sites to `split(/\r?\n/)`. Add one `test()` that builds the CRLF variant of the routing and overrides text and compares the extractor outputs. No shipped plugin file changes. The markdown inputs stay byte-identical.

Alternative rejected: a `.gitattributes` `eol=lf` rule for `*.md`. It would change checkout behavior for every Windows user of the repo, and the only current `.gitattributes` rule is a narrow fixture-hash carve-out. `readText()` is the convention #2763 and #3113 settled on.

### Key Files

- `tests/manifesto-overrides-ceiling-conformance.test.js` — use `readText()` for the three reads, split on `/\r?\n/`, add the CRLF case
- `tests/helpers/read-skill.js` — unchanged; existing `readText()` helper being consumed
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-routing.md` — unchanged; read-only input (the ceiling-keyed routing table at line 45)
- `plugin/skills/flow/manifesto-overrides.md` — unchanged; read-only input
- `plugin/skills/flow/manifesto.md` — unchanged; read-only input

## Gotchas

- Scope is this one file. Sibling "Windows regression: N test file(s) newly failing after …" records each cover their own files. The project skill also asks for a grep of `tests/` for the same `split('\n')` + exact-line-match shape. Any further instance found that no open Windows-regression record already names goes to `/claude-tweaks:capture`, not into this change.
- ubuntu CI cannot see this class of failure. The CRLF case in Deliverable 3 is the Linux-runnable pin. Without it, a later edit could reintroduce the raw read and stay green on every PR.
- The backtick-quoted cells in the header literal must stay byte-exact. Only the line terminator is the problem, so do not loosen the header match to a regex.

groups.body:
Surface: infra

**Related:** #3429, #3440, #3505, #2713, #3187, #3396, #3506, #3507, #3517, #3518, #3523, #2767

## Current State

The post-merge `windows-regression` workflow (run 39101919451, on `windows-latest`) found one test file newly failing after PR #3445 merged as `5fe0d5329`. PR #3445 shipped #3161, which made `plugin/skills/specify/record-creation-subissues.md`'s cross-reference fence set `$SPECIFY_DECOMP_MANIFEST` itself and added `tests/specify-crossref-manifest-resolve.test.js` to pin it. Verdict line: `Baseline: adjudicated against 7a649060e — 102 failing file(s): 101 also fail at base, 0 flaky (passed in isolation), 1 attributable`. The run's TAP log shows `ok 11371` (the string-pin test), `not ok 11372` (the standalone-run test), and `ok 11373` (the go-red control). Verified against `origin/main` at `7852fd8bf`, where neither the test file nor the skill file has changed since `5fe0d5329`.

The skill text is correct. The defect is in the test fixture:

- `tests/specify-crossref-manifest-resolve.test.js:15` sets `PLUGIN_ROOT = path.join(REPO_ROOT, 'plugin')`, which is native, so on the runner it is `D:\a\claude-tweaks\claude-tweaks\plugin`. Line 51 passes it unchanged as `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` in the env of each `bash -c` fence run.
- Every fence the test runs (the init, accumulate, and cross-reference fences in `record-creation-subissues.md`, near lines 15, 171 and 190) interpolates `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` into a JavaScript single-quoted literal inside `node -e "..."`: `require('${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/lib/session-tmp.js')`. Bash keeps the backslashes inside double quotes, and JS then reads `\a`, `\c` and `\p` as escapes and drops them. The result is `Cannot find module 'D:aclaude-tweaksclaude-tweaksplugin/bin/lib/session-tmp.js'`. Reproduced on macOS by running that fence shape with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT='D:\a\claude-tweaks\claude-tweaks\plugin'`: it prints that exact mangled path.
- The Windows stack trace puts the failure at line 54, the **init** fence's `expectOk`, not at the cross-reference fence. The `$(node -e ...)` substitution fails, `SPECIFY_DECOMP_MANIFEST` comes out empty, and the fence's `writeFileSync('')` exits 1 with `ENOENT`.
- So the go-red control at lines 90-94 passes on Windows without testing anything. It strips the assignment from the cross-reference fence and expects `/fence exited 1: [\s\S]*ENOENT/`. On Windows the init fence already throws that, so the stripped fence never runs. On Linux the control does what it says.

Prior art for exactly this class: PR #3076 fixed `tests/dispatch-not-spec-shaped-exclusion-fixture.test.js:69` the same way, passing `path.join(ROOT, 'plugin').split(path.sep).join('/')` because "the snippet interpolates this into a JS string literal, where a win32 backslash path would be read as escapes". `tests/adopted-branch-collision-snippet-fixture.test.js:23`, `tests/backlog-refine-foldin-no-truncation.test.js:26` and `tests/backlog-overview-foldin-no-truncation.test.js:25` define their `PLUGIN_ROOT` in that forward-slash form. #3076's PR body records that the harness substitutes a forward-slash plugin root at runtime, so the shipped fences are unaffected.

## Deliverables

1. `tests/specify-crossref-manifest-resolve.test.js`: pass `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` to the fences with forward slashes. Either define `PLUGIN_ROOT` at line 15 as `path.join(REPO_ROOT, 'plugin').split(path.sep).join('/')`, as `tests/backlog-refine-foldin-no-truncation.test.js:26` does (the `fs.readFileSync` at line 19 accepts it on every OS), or keep line 15 native and normalize only the env value at line 51. Add a one-line comment naming the JS-string-literal reason, as `tests/dispatch-not-spec-shaped-exclusion-fixture.test.js:67-68` does.
2. Same file: make the go-red control prove that the **cross-reference** fence failed. Today the regex `/fence exited 1: [\s\S]*ENOENT/` cannot tell which of the four fence runs threw. Name the failing step in the `expectOk` failure message inside `assertCrossrefFenceRunsStandalone` (for example `cross-reference fence exited 1: ...` versus `init fence exited 1: ...`), and anchor the go-red regex on the cross-reference step's name. Then a broken init or accumulate run can never satisfy the control.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `node --test tests/specify-crossref-manifest-resolve.test.js` passes on macOS/Linux. All three tests run, and none is skipped or removed.
- [ ] The same file passes on `windows-latest`. Prove it before merge: run `gh workflow run windows-regression.yml --ref {branch}` and quote the run's result for this file. A non-main ref never files an issue. If the dispatch cannot run, say so explicitly. A `path.win32` simulation does not count as a Windows run.
- [ ] The go-red control still discriminates, and for the right step. Temporarily run it with the init fence's assignment stripped instead of the cross-reference fence's. The control must go **red**, because the failure now names the init step. Restore it in the same command.
- [ ] The standalone-run test still discriminates. Temporarily delete the `SPECIFY_DECOMP_MANIFEST=$(...)` assignment from the cross-reference fence in `plugin/skills/specify/record-creation-subissues.md`. Test 2 must go red on Linux. Restore the file in the same command.
- [ ] No file under `plugin/` changes. The shipped fences already receive a forward-slash plugin root from the harness.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Fixed a /specify decomposition test that failed on Windows because it passed the plugin path with backslashes.

## Technical Approach

The fix is test-side only, following `.claude/skills/windows-checkout-test-parity/SKILL.md` and #3076's precedent. The plugin root reaches the fences as an environment variable that is interpolated into a JS string literal, so the test must hand the fences the same forward-slash form the harness supplies at runtime. This is not a display ID versus native path question: the value is never opened natively by the fence's shell, it is source text for `node -e`. For the go-red tightening, the cheapest change is a step label threaded through the `run`/`expectOk` helpers in `assertCrossrefFenceRunsStandalone`. The test's own string-pin test (lines 69-84) stays as it is.

### Key Files

- `tests/specify-crossref-manifest-resolve.test.js`: `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` passed with forward slashes (line 15 or 51), plus the go-red control (lines 90-94) anchored on the failing step's name
- `plugin/skills/specify/record-creation-subissues.md`: read-only reference. The init, accumulate and cross-reference fences the test extracts and runs (near lines 15, 171 and 190)
- `tests/dispatch-not-spec-shaped-exclusion-fixture.test.js`: read-only reference. #3076's forward-slash precedent (line 69)

## Gotchas

- Do not "fix" this by changing the skill fences to read `process.env.CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` or by normalizing in `plugin/`. The harness already substitutes a forward-slash root (#3076), so the shipped prose works. Only the test's fixture env differs from what the harness provides.
- `tests/specify-ceremony-tally-prose.test.js` runs the same init and accumulate fences with the same unnormalized `PLUGIN_ROOT` (line 74 feeding line 104). It is not this record's failure: it already fails at base on Windows, earlier, at module load. Its `fenceAfter` reads the skill without CRLF normalization (`extraction pattern is out of sync: no bash fence after **Fresh manifest for this invocation.**`), so it was adjudicated as also failing at base. Fixing the CRLF read would expose this same plugin-root failure there. Keep it out of this PR. During the build, check whether a record already covers it (the #2767 umbrella baseline record is the likely home), and file one via `/claude-tweaks:capture` if none does.
- On `windows-latest` the checkout is on `D:` and `os.tmpdir()` on `C:`. The fixture's scratch `root` lives under tmp while `PLUGIN_ROOT` is on the checkout drive. Mixing drives is fine here because nothing compares the two paths. Do not hard-code a drive or root in any expected value.
- This is one of several open `Windows regression:` records (#3429, #3440, #3505, #3506, #3507, #3517, #3518, #3523), each for a different commit and different files. Keep this record to `tests/specify-crossref-manifest-resolve.test.js`.

The post-merge Windows check failed on commit 5fe0d532902beecac9fc337a7a86820640d27840 (compared against 7a649060e).

groups.body:
Surface: backend

**Related:** #3049, #2955, #3001

## Current State

`/claude-tweaks:review` Step 3 has the orchestrator write two kinds of coordination input into `{ctx-dir}`, the scratch dir `build-review-context.js build` mints:

- `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md` (Reproduction dispatch, Mode 1): after both agents of a pair return, "write each agent's `findings` array to `{ctx-dir}/lens-{LENS}-agentA.json` / `{ctx-dir}/lens-{LENS}-agentB.json`", then `review-coordination.js categorise-reproduction` reads those two paths.
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-debate-and-refutation.md` (step 1, Detect overlap): the `{lensName: [findings...]}` object is written to `{ctx-dir}/findings-by-lens.json` for `review-coordination.js detect-overlap`.

Under `--run "$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR"`, `{ctx-dir}` is `{run}/review-ctx`, inside the **main checkout** (the run dir is anchored there). A session isolated to a linked worktree (dispatch's two-call handoff, `worktree-always`) is refused both ways of writing there. The `Write` tool is refused by cross-checkout write pinning ("Edit the worktree copy of this file instead"), and a Bash heredoc redirect is refused by the Claude Code harness's worktree-isolation guard as "too complex to verify". Reported on 6.133.0: 3 refused tool calls in an unattended run. The working workaround was writing the JSON elsewhere and passing those paths, which works because both `review-coordination.js` subcommands already take arbitrary file paths (`plugin/bin/review-coordination.js:55-75`).

## Deliverables

1. **Decision (approved in brainstorming, 2026-10-15):** these coordination inputs are written to the session-scoped temp dir (`plugin/skills/_shared/session-tmp-root.md`), never into `{ctx-dir}`, under every session, not only isolated ones. That dir is outside every checkout, so the `Write` tool is never refused there. No sanctioned-writer CLI and no stdin input: stdin would need the JSON in a shell literal or heredoc, the shape the harness guard refuses.
2. `step3-lens-dispatch.md` Reproduction dispatch: resolve each pair's two paths via `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/session-tmp-resolve.js"`. The names carry the review's own `{ctx-dir}` basename (`review-{ctx-id}-lens-{LENS}-agentA.json` / `…-agentB.json`), so concurrent reviews in one session (dispatched subagents share `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`) never collide. Then `Write` the arrays there and pass those paths to `categorise-reproduction`.
3. `step3-debate-and-refutation.md` step 1: same treatment for `findings-by-lens.json` (`review-{ctx-id}-findings-by-lens.json`) before `detect-overlap`. The existing "never a fixed shared `/tmp` name" rationale is kept and satisfied by the per-review name.
4. `step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s Agent-scratch cleanup check: the `{ctx-dir}` exclusion list drops `lens-*.json` and `findings-by-lens.json`, which no longer live there, and keeps the pre/post-fan-out status snapshots. The `git status … > {ctx-dir}/pre-dispatch-status.txt` redirect stays (a plain redirect, not refused).
5. A conformance assertion in `tests/bin-lib/review-context/prose.test.js`: neither step file directs writing `lens-*.json` or `findings-by-lens.json` into `{ctx-dir}`, and both name the session-scoped temp dir for them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `step3-lens-dispatch.md` contains no instruction to write `lens-{LENS}-agent{A,B}.json` under `{ctx-dir}`. Its `categorise-reproduction` invocation takes session-scoped temp paths whose names include the `{ctx-dir}` basename.
- [ ] `step3-debate-and-refutation.md` contains no instruction to write `findings-by-lens.json` under `{ctx-dir}`. Its `detect-overlap` invocation takes a session-scoped temp path including the `{ctx-dir}` basename.
- [ ] The Agent-scratch cleanup check's `{ctx-dir}` exclusion list no longer names `lens-*.json` / `findings-by-lens.json`.
- [ ] The new `prose.test.js` assertions fail against today's `origin/main` text and pass after the change (red first).
- [ ] No change to `plugin/bin/review-coordination.js` or `plugin/bin/build-review-context.js`.
- [ ] `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Code review no longer stalls on refused file writes when it runs in an isolated worktree session.

## Technical Approach

Prose-only change to two review step files plus one conformance test. The pattern is the one `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console.md` already uses for `set-verify-expectations.js --file`: write the JSON with the `Write` tool to the session scratchpad, outside both `$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR` and the worktree, then hand the path to a CLI. The difference here is that no copy back into the run dir is needed, because `categorise-reproduction`/`detect-overlap` consume the files directly and their results already land in `decisions.md` and the routing entries. Resolve paths with the existing `bin/session-tmp-resolve.js` (`NAME=filename` pairs → shell exports), in the same Bash call that uses them, since no shell variable survives across calls.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md` — Reproduction dispatch write target, `categorise-reproduction` invocation, Agent-scratch cleanup exclusion list
- `plugin/skills/review/step3-debate-and-refutation.md` — step 1 `findings-by-lens.json` write target and `detect-overlap` invocation
- `tests/bin-lib/review-context/prose.test.js` — new conformance assertions

## Gotchas

- Dispatched subagents share one `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, so a bare `lens-3a-agentA.json` in the session temp dir *would* collide across two concurrent dispatched reviews. The `{ctx-dir}` basename in every name is what keeps them apart, so don't drop it.
- `{ctx-dir}` itself is unchanged: the context bundle and status snapshots stay under `{run}/review-ctx`. Only the orchestrator-written coordination inputs move.
- The refusal is the harness's own worktree-isolation guard plus the `Write` tool's cross-checkout pinning, not plugin code (same finding as #2548). The fix routes around both, and nothing upstream is filed from this record.
- `tests/multi-agent-coordination.test.js` reads both step files. Re-run it after the edit in case it pins the old `{ctx-dir}/lens-…` wording.

## Original request

review lens dispatch: a worktree-isolated session cannot write the {ctx-dir}/lens-*.json findings files

**Summary:** Step 3 asks for each agent's findings to be written to `{ctx-dir}/lens-{LENS}-agent{A,B}.json`. When `{ctx-dir}` sits under the run directory anchored to the main checkout, a session isolated to a linked worktree is refused both the Write tool and a heredoc.

**Kind:** Gap

**Affected component:** claude-tweaks review, `skills/review/step3-lens-dispatch.md` (reproduction dispatch), together with `bin/build-review-context.js --run` and `bin/review-coordination.js categorise-reproduction`

**Use case:** A `/claude-tweaks:flow` review step ran in a worktree-isolated session, as dispatch's two-call handoff does. `build-review-context.js build --run <run-dir>` placed `{ctx-dir}` under `<run-dir>/review-ctx`, inside the main checkout. Writing the `lens-*.json` files there failed two ways. The Write tool was refused by cross-checkout write pinning ("Edit the worktree copy of this file instead"). A Bash heredoc redirect to the same path was refused by the worktree-isolation guard as "too complex to verify". The workaround was to write the JSON to the system temp dir and pass those paths to `categorise-reproduction`. `stage-item.js` exists for `staged/`, but nothing equivalent exists for review-ctx scratch files. Cost: 3 refused tool calls, about 2 minutes, in an otherwise unattended run. Possible fixes: a sanctioned writer (a `review-coordination.js` subcommand that takes the findings on stdin and writes `{ctx-dir}/lens-*.json` itself), or `categorise-reproduction` accepting both findings arrays on stdin.

**Definition:** Needed — the two possible fixes (a sanctioned writer, or stdin input to categorise-reproduction) are both viable and no choice has been made.

**Plugin version:** 6.133.0

groups.body:
Surface: backend

## Overview

Part of the "Build dispatch cost shape" decomposition (origin #3229). In the measured 10-task build, two implement-and-review cycles would have been saved by combining small adjacent tasks — for example "add a column" followed by "a pure function over it", or "add a job" followed by "remove what it replaces". Each separate task costs an implementer dispatch and a task review even when the second task only consumes the first's output.

This record adds plan-authoring guidance: when two adjacent tasks touch the same files, the second only consumes the first's output, and neither needs its own review surface, the author writes them as one task. This is plan granularity, not SDD's batch rule: it needs no marker, adds no tier or dispatch instruction, and does not interact with `plan-audit.js --count-tasks`' `batched` flag. It sits next to, and cross-references, the fast-lane transcription batching guidance from #3123.

**Complexity:** Low
**Estimated tasks:** 2-3

## Non-Goals

- A new plan marker, a dispatch change, or any change to what `dispatch.md` forwards to SDD.
- Changing the `batched` flag, `--count-tasks`, or the roster row `sdd-whole-branch-review`.
- Re-steering plans already written; the guidance applies to plans authored after it ships.
- Overriding SDD's one-dispatch-per-task default for work that needs its own judgment, its own tests or its own review surface (SDD's "Reserve one-dispatch-per-task" clause stays the rule for those).

## Prerequisites

| Record | Title | Status |
|--------|-------|--------|
| #3123 | build / subagent-driven-development dispatch: fast-lane multi-task transcription plans still pay a review for every task plus a whole-branch review | ready — extends the same Batched-plan marker paragraph in the same file; this record lands after it and cross-references it |
| #3310 | Cut every skill-size consumer over to the rail, load delta, and size outlier | ready, in progress — shares `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` |

## Current State

- `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` (33,050 bytes of a 51,200-byte shared ceiling) — a list of plan-authoring checks; the Batched-plan marker paragraph says that when a plan bundles several same-shape edits into one dispatch (SDD's "Batch small same-shape work"), the author writes `**Execution:** batched` in the plan header or `[batch]` in the task title, and that `plan-audit.js --count-tasks` reads exactly those two markers.
- #3123 (ready) extends that paragraph with fast-lane transcription-plan batching guidance and adds pins in `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/parser.test.js` and `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js`.
- `plugin/bin/lib/plan-audit/parser.js` — `countTasks` reads `{ tasks, batched }`; a plan's task count is whatever `### Task N:` headings it contains, so merging two tasks into one simply lowers `tasks`.
- SDD 7.0.0 `## The Task Loop`: "Batch small same-shape work … Reserve one-dispatch-per-task for work that needs its own judgment, its own tests, or its own review surface."
- Tests that pin prose in this file: `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js` (the Batched-plan paragraph) and the Byte-pin check in the file itself.

## Deliverables

- [ ] A new paragraph (or an extension placed directly adjacent to the Batched-plan marker paragraph) in `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md`: when two adjacent tasks touch the same files, the second only builds on the first's output (consumes it, or is made safe by it), and the second adds no separately reviewable surface (no behavior or test a reviewer would judge on its own), write them as ONE task; worked examples that pass those conditions ("add a column" plus the one-line type or constant that exposes it; "add a job" plus "remove the code it replaces"; "add a column" plus "a pure function over it" only when both tasks' tests sit in the same test file the first task already edits).
- [ ] The guidance states what it is not: not SDD's batch rule, no marker, no effect on `--count-tasks`' `batched` flag, and the exclusion list (the second task has tests or behavior of its own that a reviewer would judge separately, touches different files, or is independently risky). It also states the one interaction with `--count-tasks`: the `tasks` count drops, and under `ceremony-profile: fast-lane` a plan that reaches `tasks: 1` with `batched: false` skips the whole-branch review (roster tag `sdd-whole-branch-review`), so an author must not merge a multi-task plan down to a single task merely to reach that skip; merge only while at least two tasks remain.
- [ ] A cross-reference to #3123's fast-lane transcription batching guidance in the same file, naming whatever heading or paragraph #3123 actually shipped (resolved at build time from the merged file), so an author reading either paragraph sees the other and knows which situation each covers (same-shape edits across files and fast-lane transcription plans there; sequential same-file tasks here).
- [ ] A prose pin in a conformance test following the neighbouring pattern (`tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js` or a small sibling) that pins the three conditions, the exclusion clauses and the "no marker, no `batched` change" statement, each with a go-red proof that the assertion fails when that clause is removed.
- [ ] The Byte-pin check run and its measured headroom reported for `plan-authoring-checks.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` contains the new guidance, which names all three conditions (adjacent tasks touching the same files, the second only building on the first's output, the second adding no separately reviewable surface) and gives examples that satisfy them.
2. The guidance states that merging produces plain plan granularity with no marker and no change to `plan-audit.js --count-tasks`' `batched` value, states the `tasks`-count interaction with the single-task fast-lane skip and the "keep at least two tasks" rule, and a parser regression test shows a merged plan prints the expected `tasks` count and `batched: false` unless a batched marker is present (a guard only: it is green before the guidance exists).
3. The new text cross-references #3123's guidance by the heading it shipped in the same file, and the Batched-plan marker paragraph from #3123 is unchanged in wording by this record.
4. A conformance assertion pins the three conditions, the exclusion clauses and the "no marker" statement; removing any one of them from the doctored text turns the assertion red.
5. `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` stays under 51,200 bytes and under any tighter pin the Byte-pin check finds; `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Added plan-authoring guidance to write small adjacent same-file tasks as one task, cutting redundant implement-and-review cycles in multi-task builds.

## Technical Approach

Prose only plus one pin test. Place the paragraph immediately after the Batched-plan marker paragraph (as #3123 leaves it), so the two granularity rules sit together. Keep it short: the file is dense and several paragraphs in it are test-pinned, so add a new paragraph rather than rewording an existing one.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` — the new guidance and the cross-reference
- `tests/ceremony-profile-roster.test.js` — prose pin and go-red proof, following #3123's pin on the adjacent paragraph
- `tests/bin-lib/plan-audit/parser.test.js` — `countTasks` non-interaction case

## Gotchas

- Steering principle for the whole decomposition: claude-tweaks never files upstream with superpowers and never contradicts SDD's text. This is a plan-authoring-time steer (the #3123 precedent), not a dispatch override; it must not tell SDD to skip a review.
- Land after #3123 (ready) — same file, adjacent paragraph. Re-read the file from the merged tree first; if #3123 has not merged when this builds, stop and report rather than editing the same paragraph in parallel.
- Do not chain this record behind the per-task-tier record even though both edit `plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md`; whichever builds second rebases (an internal file-overlap conflict, flagged at decomposition time).
- Also shares the file with ready records #3079 and #3310 (in progress).
- Do not add a marker: a marker would reach `plan-audit`'s parser and risk colliding with `**Execution:** batched`, whose regex is end-anchored (`^\*\*Execution:\*\*\s*batched\s*$`). Merging tasks changes only the task count.
- A merged task still gets one task review. The guidance must not suggest that merging lets a risky change skip review; a task whose review surface is genuinely separate stays separate.
- Measure byte headroom with the file's own Byte-pin check before writing, after #3123 and any other record has merged: 18,150 bytes remain under the shared ceiling at record-writing time (a snapshot, since four records edit the file), and a tighter per-file pin may exist. Keep the new paragraph short.

groups.body:
Origin: reflect full from #3311
Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`plugin/skills/build/plan-authoring-checks.md` has no check for a plan that retires a mechanism. That covers deleting a constant, an option, a CLI or a gate.

#3311's plan copied its prose-rewrite file list from the spec's boundary amendment 4, which named three files. About 40 further shipped-skill, doc, journey and test-comment sites still cited the deleted mechanisms. They used phrasings the list never searched for: "warning tier", "40 KB ceiling", "#724 budget", "five bloat signals", `ceiling: Infinity`. The whole-branch review caught them (two Important findings), followed by two residual sweeps.

Evidence: #3311 final-review findings F1–F3 and commits 2347b6b1e, 4572f470b and 981550f92. Cost this session: one fix wave, two residual sweeps and a scoped re-review.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Add a "Retirement sweep" check to `plan-authoring-checks.md`. When a plan deletes a named mechanism, it must carry a task that sweeps every non-history path in the repo for each phrasing of that mechanism: the identifier, the file path, the option literal, the numeric value as prose, and the issue number used as a label. The task's verification grep must name each phrasing.
- [ ] Cite the existing memory rules ("Deleted-rule citation sweep", "Grep retired term repo-wide") as the rationale.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `plan-authoring-checks.md` names the retirement-sweep check, and a conformance test pins its presence.
2. The check says the sweep's file list comes from the grep's output, never from the spec's named list.

## Release Note

No user-visible change; `/build`'s plan-authoring checks gain a retirement-sweep check, so a plan that deletes a mechanism also sweeps every phrasing of it.
